+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""Orchestrator for the ai-review POC (RFC #21451).
+
+State machine summary (states persist in the agent's own last PR comment via
+a machine-readable signature block, no external storage):
+
+    <!-- ai-review: state=reviewing | round=1/5 | total=1 | head=abc1234 -->
+
+    labeled(ai-review, by write user)   -> round 1 agent review
+    author push (synchronize)           -> revoke `ai-review-passed`, re-review
+    author comment with /ai-review      -> next round (ignores plain comments)
+    reviewer removes label /ai-review-stop -> stopped, the agent stays silent
+
+Termination: pass verdict (MUST-FIX == 0), per-push round cap (5), reviewer
+stop, waiting-human decision, whole-PR budget cap (15). The agent never
+approves; `ai-review-passed` is not an approve.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import argparse
+import fnmatch
+import json
+import os
+import subprocess
+import sys
+import time
+from dataclasses import dataclass
+
+import regex as re
+import yaml
+
+AI_REVIEW_LABEL = "ai-review"
+AI_REVIEW_PASSED_LABEL = "ai-review-passed"
+# Slash command style, consistent with the repo's other PR commands (/e2e,
+# /rerun, ...): no account is implied. The negative lookahead keeps
+# `/ai-review-stop` and hypothetical `/ai-reviewer` from matching.
+MENTION_RE = re.compile(r"/ai-review(?![\w-])")
+STOP_RE = re.compile(r"/ai-review-stop(?![\w-])")
+BOT_MARKER = "ai-review-orchestrator"
+SIGNATURE_RE = re.compile(r"<!-- ai-review: ([^>]+) -->")
+FIELD_RE = re.compile(r"(\w+)=(\S+)")
+MAX_ROUNDS_PER_PUSH = 5
+MAX_TOTAL_ROUNDS = 15
+
+
+def parse_allowlist(text: str) -> set[str]:
+    """Usernames from the allowlist; `#` starts a comment anywhere."""
+    entries = set()
+    for line in text.splitlines():
+        user = line.split("#", 1)[0].strip()
+        if user:
+            entries.add(user)
+    return entries
+
+
+# Cost guards. A several-thousand-line diff (recipes, overlays, .po files)
+# dominates the per-round token bill, and an agent left unbounded can wander
+# for half an hour; cap both.
+MAX_DIFF_CHARS = 80_000
+ROUND_TIMEOUT_SECONDS = 600
+
+
+def render_template(template: str, values: dict[str, str]) -> str:
+    """Single-pass {{PLACEHOLDER}} substitution.
+
+    Values are never re-scanned, so a diff containing something that looks
+    like a placeholder cannot inject other values; unknown placeholders are
+    left verbatim so a template typo is visible in the output.
+    """
+    return re.sub(
+        r"\{\{(\w+)\}\}",
+        lambda m: values.get(m.group(1), m.group(0)),
+        template,
+    )
+
+
+def truncate_diff(diff: str, limit: int = MAX_DIFF_CHARS) -> str:
+    """Cap the diff so one huge PR cannot dominate the token bill; the
+    agent is told to read the remainder from the head/ checkout."""
+    if len(diff) <= limit:
+        return diff
+    cut = diff[:limit]
+    # keep the truncation boundary on a line edge
+    cut = cut[: cut.rfind("\n") + 1]
+    return (
+        cut
+        + f"\n\n[diff truncated at {limit} characters; "
+        + f"{len(diff) - len(cut)} more characters — read the remaining "
+        + "changed files directly from head/ if needed]\n"
+    )
+
+
+def resolve_domains(domains_yaml: str, files: list[str]) -> list[dict]:
+    """Match changed PR files against the coarse domains.yaml registry.
+
+    fnmatch's `*` crosses `/`, so a glob like `.github/**` matches nested
+    paths — which is what the coarse registry wants. First match wins.
+    """
+    try:
+        registry = yaml.safe_load(domains_yaml) or {}
+    except yaml.YAMLError as exc:
+        print(f"::warning::domains.yaml is invalid, no L2 domains resolve: {exc}")
+        return []
+    matched = []
+    for domain in registry.get("domains", []):
+        globs = domain.get("paths", [])
+        if any(fnmatch.fnmatch(f, g) for f in files for g in globs):
+            matched.append(domain)
+    return matched
+
+
+# The agent signals "all MUST-FIX resolved" with this marker line, which the
+# orchestrator (not the agent itself) turns into the `ai-review-passed` label.
+
+PASS_MARKER = "AI-REVIEW-VERDICT: PASS"
+
+# The agent emits each finding as a fenced block; the orchestrator turns the
+# parsed ones into inline review comments anchored on the code line.
+FINDING_BLOCK_RE = re.compile(r"```finding\n(.*?)```", re.S)
+FIELD_LINE_RE = re.compile(r"^(\w+):\s*(.+)$", re.M)
+REQUIRED_FINDING_FIELDS = ("path", "line", "severity", "rule", "body")
+
+# Marker embedded in every inline finding comment so thread replies can be
+# attributed to the agent, and so waived findings stay visibly marked.
+INLINE_MARKER = "ai-review finding"
+WAIVED_PREFIX = "**[WAIVED"
+WAIVE_RE = re.compile(r"/ai-review-waive(?![\w-])")
+
+
+def parse_findings(text: str) -> list[dict]:
+    """Parse ```finding blocks into dicts; malformed blocks are dropped.
+
+    `body` is everything after its key line (multi-line allowed); the other
+    fields are single `key: value` lines before it.
+    """
+    findings = []
+    for m in FINDING_BLOCK_RE.finditer(text):
+        block = m.group(1)
+        body_match = re.search(r"^body:\s*(.*)$", block, re.M)
+        if not body_match:
+            continue
+        fields = dict(FIELD_LINE_RE.findall(block[: body_match.start()]))
+        # body is the key line's remainder plus everything after it, so it
+        # may span multiple lines; strip each piece, then re-join
+        fields["body"] = "\n".join(
+            part.strip() for part in (body_match.group(1), block[body_match.end() :]) if part.strip()
+        )
+        if not all(f in fields and fields[f].strip() for f in REQUIRED_FINDING_FIELDS):
+            continue
+        try:
+            line = int(fields["line"])
+        except ValueError:
+            continue
+        if line < 1:
+            continue
+        findings.append(
+            {
+                "path": fields["path"].strip(),
+                "line": line,
+                "severity": fields["severity"].strip(),
+                "rule": fields["rule"].strip(),
+                "body": fields["body"].strip(),
+            }
+        )
+    return findings
+
+
+def post_inline_review(pr: int, head_sha: str, findings: list[dict]) -> bool:
+    """Post one COMMENT-level review with the findings as inline comments.
+
+    Returns False if GitHub rejected the anchors (e.g. a line outside the
+    diff context), in which case the caller falls back to the summary.
+    """
+    comments = []
+    for f in findings:
+        body = (
+            f"**[{f['severity']}]** rule: `{f['rule']}`\n\n{f['body']}\n\n"
+            "🤖 ai-review finding — `ai-review-passed` is not an approve."
+        )
+        comments.append({"path": f["path"], "line": f["line"], "side": "RIGHT", "body": body})
+    payload = {
+        "commit_id": head_sha,
+        "event": "COMMENT",
+        "body": f"🤖 ai-review round: {len(findings)} finding(s) anchored inline.",
+        "comments": comments,
+    }
+    with open("/tmp/ai-review-payload.json", "w") as fp:
+        json.dump(payload, fp)
+    result = subprocess.run(
+        ["gh", "api", "--input", "/tmp/ai-review-payload.json", f"repos/:owner/:repo/pulls/{pr}/reviews"],
+        capture_output=True,
+        text=True,
+    )
+    if result.returncode != 0:
+        print(f"::warning::inline review rejected, falling back to summary: {result.stderr.strip()[:300]}", flush=True)
+        return False
+    return True
+
+
+@dataclass
+class State:
+    state: str = "none"
+    round: int = 0
+    total: int = 0
+    head: str = ""
+
+    def signature(self, head: str) -> str:
+        self.head = head
+        fields = " | ".join(
+            f"{k}={v}"
+            for k, v in (
+                ("state", self.state),
+                ("round", f"{self.round}/{MAX_ROUNDS_PER_PUSH}"),
+                ("total", self.total),
+                ("head", self.head),
+            )
+        )
+        return f"<!-- ai-review: {fields} -->"
+
+
+class Orchestrator:
+    def __init__(self, workspace: str, pr: int, event: str, actor: str, comment_body: str):
+        self.workspace = workspace
+        self.pr = pr
+        self.event = event  # e.g. "pull_request_target/labeled"
+        self.actor = actor
+        self.comment_body = comment_body
+        self.head_sha = self._gh("pr", "view", str(pr), "--json", "headRefOid", "-q", ".headRefOid")
+        self.state = self._load_state()
+
+    # ---- thin gh wrappers -------------------------------------------------
+
+    def _gh(self, *args: str) -> str:
+        return subprocess.run(["gh", *args], check=True, capture_output=True, text=True).stdout.strip()
+
+    def _gh_json(self, *args: str):
+        return json.loads(self._gh(*args))
+
+    def comment(self, body: str):
+        subprocess.run(
+            ["gh", "pr", "comment", str(self.pr), "--body-file", "-"],
+            input=body + "\n",
+            check=True,
+            text=True,
+        )
+
+    # ---- state ------------------------------------------------------------
+
+    def _load_state(self) -> State:
+        comments = self._gh_json(
+            "pr",
+            "view",
+            str(self.pr),
+            "--json",
+            "comments",
+            "-q",
+            ".comments",
+        )
+        for c in reversed(comments):
+            m = SIGNATURE_RE.search(c.get("body", ""))
+            if not m:
+                continue
+            fields = dict(FIELD_RE.findall(m.group(1)))
+            return State(
+                state=fields.get("state", "none"),
+                round=int(fields.get("round", "0/5").split("/")[0]),
+                total=int(fields.get("total", "0")),
+                head=fields.get("head", ""),
+            )
+        return State()
+
+    # ---- gates ------------------------------------------------------------
+
+    def actor_can_write(self) -> bool:
+        perm = self._gh_json("api", f"repos/:owner/:repo/collaborators/{self.actor}/permission")
+        return perm.get("permission") in ("admin", "maintain", "write")
+
+    def author_in_allowlist(self) -> bool:
+        author = self._gh("pr", "view", str(self.pr), "--json", "author", "-q", ".author.login")
+        path = os.path.join(self.workspace, ".github", "agent-review", "allowlist.txt")
+        with open(path) as f:
+            entries = parse_allowlist(f.read())
+        return author in entries
+
+    # ---- agent round ------------------------------------------------------
+
+    def run_agent_round(self, round_no: int, closing: bool = False):
+        """Assemble the prompt and let the agent produce its next comment.
+
+        Progressive disclosure: the prompt carries the instructions and a
+        knowledge-base MAP only; the agent reads full checklist files itself
+        from the checked-out workspace (they live under
+        .github/agent-review/, inside the repo the job checked out).
+        """
+        with open(os.path.join(self.workspace, ".github", "agent-review", "instructions.md")) as f:
+            instructions = f.read()
+        kb_map = self._knowledge_base_map()
+        diff = truncate_diff(self._gh("pr", "diff", str(self.pr)))
+        prev_agent_comment = self._last_agent_comment_text()
+        user_reply = self.comment_body or "(n/a — new push or first round)"
+        domains = self._touched_domains()
+        waived = self._waived_findings()
+
+        closing_note = ""
+        if closing:
+            closing_note = (
+                "\nThis is the FINAL round for this push (round cap reached). "
+                "Do NOT raise new findings. Produce a closing summary listing "
+                "every unresolved finding and what a human reviewer must decide, "
+                "then set state=waiting-human.\n"
+            )
+
+        # The prompt skeleton lives in
+        # .github/agent-review/prompt_template.md (owner-gated with the rest
+        # of the knowledge base); this code only fills in the values.
+        template_path = os.path.join(self.workspace, ".github", "agent-review", "prompt_template.md")
+        with open(template_path) as f:
+            template = f.read()
+        waived_section = (
+            "\n\n## Waived findings (human decision — FINAL, do not re-raise, "
+            "do not count toward MUST-FIX)\n\n" + "\n".join(f"- {w}" for w in waived)
+            if waived
+            else ""
+        )
+        domains_section = (
+            "\n".join(f"- {d['name']}: {d.get('description', '')} — read `L2/{d['name']}/` first" for d in domains)
+            or "(none matched — L1 global rules only)"
+        )
+        prompt = render_template(
+            template,
+            {
+                "INSTRUCTIONS": instructions.strip(),
+                "ENVIRONMENT": (
+                    "## Working environment\n\n"
+                    "- Your working directory is a full checkout of the"
+                    " vllm-ascend repository (BASE branch).\n"
+                    "- The PR's own code is checked out read-only under"
+                    " `head/`. Finding line numbers refer to files under"
+                    " `head/` — when you need context around a changed line,"
+                    " read the file at `head/<path>`, never from the base"
+                    " checkout.\n"
+                    "- Project documentation lives under `head/docs/source/`;"
+                    " the contributor guidelines are `head/AGENTS.md`"
+                    " (background only — the review rules are the checklists"
+                    " in the knowledge base map).\n"
+                    "- Knowledge base map paths are relative to the working"
+                    " directory (the trusted BASE checkout).\n"
+                    "- You have read access to all of it. Do not modify,"
+                    " build or execute anything; this is a review-only"
+                    " environment.\n"
+                ),
+                "KB_MAP": kb_map.strip(),
+                "WAIVED_SECTION": waived_section,
+                "DOMAINS": domains_section,
+                "HEAD_SHA": self.head_sha[:12],
+                "DIFF": diff.strip(),
+                "PREV_COMMENT": prev_agent_comment or "(first round)",
+                "REPLY": user_reply,
+                "CLOSING_NOTE": closing_note,
+                "ROUND": round_no,
+                "MAX_ROUNDS": MAX_ROUNDS_PER_PUSH,
+                "TOTAL": self.state.total + 1,
+                "MAX_TOTAL": MAX_TOTAL_ROUNDS,
+            },
+        )
+        leftover = re.findall(r"\{\{\w+\}\}", prompt)
+        if leftover:
+            print(
+                f"::warning::unfilled prompt placeholders: {sorted(set(leftover))}",
+                flush=True,
+            )
+
+        prompt_file = "/tmp/ai-review-prompt.md"
+        out_file = "/tmp/ai-review-output.md"
+        with open(prompt_file, "w") as f:
+            f.write(prompt)
+
+        cmd = os.environ.get("AI_REVIEW_DSH_CMD", "dsh --profile headless").split()
+        # The agent process gets ONLY the model credentials and the model
+        # name — never GH_TOKEN. Every GitHub API call is made by this
+        # orchestrator; the agent's output is parsed text we post ourselves.
+        # This keeps a prompt-injected PR diff from reaching any repo token.
+        env = {
+            "PATH": os.environ.get("PATH", "/usr/bin:/bin"),
+            "HOME": os.environ.get("HOME", "/tmp"),
+            "AI_REVIEW_KEY": os.environ.get("AI_REVIEW_KEY", ""),
+            "AI_REVIEW_API": os.environ.get("AI_REVIEW_API", ""),
+            # Picked up by dsh's config surface once confirmed in the smoke
+            # test; harmless to expose until then.
+            "AI_REVIEW_MODEL": os.environ.get("AI_REVIEW_MODEL", "deepseek-v4.1-flash"),
+        }
+        started = time.monotonic()
+        print(
+            f"::notice::ai-review prompt size: {len(prompt)} chars; "
+            f"engine: {cmd[0]}; timeout: {ROUND_TIMEOUT_SECONDS}s",
+            flush=True,
+        )
+        try:
+            with open(out_file, "w") as out:
+                subprocess.run(
+                    [*cmd, prompt_file],
+                    stdout=out,
+                    check=True,
+                    env=env,
+                    timeout=ROUND_TIMEOUT_SECONDS,
+                )
+        except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
+            # Budget is NOT consumed: the state signature is re-posted
+            # unchanged so the author can retry after the engine is fixed.
+            print(
+                f"::error::agent round exceeded {ROUND_TIMEOUT_SECONDS}s and was aborted",
+                flush=True,
+            )
+            self.post_notice(
+                f"⏱️ AI review round aborted: the agent exceeded "
+                f"{ROUND_TIMEOUT_SECONDS // 60} minutes. No review was produced "
+                "and the round budget was not consumed. Retry with `/ai-review`.",
+                new_state=State(
+                    state=self.state.state,
+                    round=self.state.round,
+                    total=self.state.total,
+                ),
+            )
+            return
+        print(
+            f"::notice::agent round finished in {time.monotonic() - started:.0f}s",
+            flush=True,
+        )
+
+        with open(out_file) as f:
+            output = f.read()
+        # Defense in depth: the agent never sees repo tokens (filtered env
+        # above), but the model key could still be coaxed into its output by
+        # an injected instruction — redact known secret values before the
+        # text ever reaches a public PR comment.
+        for secret_name in ("AI_REVIEW_KEY", "AI_REVIEW_API", "GH_TOKEN"):
+            secret_value = os.environ.get(secret_name, "")
+            if secret_value:
+                output = output.replace(secret_value, "***REDACTED***")
+        verdict_pass = PASS_MARKER in output
+
+        new_state = State(state="reviewing", round=round_no, total=self.state.total + 1)
+        if closing:
+            new_state.state = "waiting-human"
+        elif verdict_pass:
+            new_state.state = "passed"
+
+        if not SIGNATURE_RE.search(output):
+            # The agent forgot the signature; append one so the next round can
+            # still restore state. Never leave the machine without a marker.
+            output += "\n\n" + new_state.signature(self.head_sha)
+        else:
+            output = SIGNATURE_RE.sub(new_state.signature(self.head_sha), output, count=1)
+
+        # Stop semantics: removing the label mid-round must win. The queued
+        # unlabeled handler runs after us and marks state=stopped; here we
+        # only need to not post a round the reviewer already cancelled. The
+        # completed round is discarded (cost is sunk, the output is dropped).
+        labels = self._gh_json("pr", "view", str(self.pr), "--json", "labels", "-q", "[.labels[].name]")
+        if AI_REVIEW_LABEL not in labels:
+            print("ai-review label was removed mid-round; discarding output", flush=True)
+            return
+
+        banner = (
+            f"<!-- {BOT_MARKER} -->\n"
+            f"🤖 **AI review** (round {round_no}/{MAX_ROUNDS_PER_PUSH}, "
+            f"engine: DeepSeek Harness headless, POC gray release — "
+            f"`ai-review-passed` is **not** an approve; human review is still required.)\n\n"
+        )
+
+        # Inline review comments: findings anchored to code lines land in one
+        # COMMENT-level review (never APPROVE); the summary comment keeps the
+        # verdict, checklist and state signature. If the review API rejects
+        # an anchor (line outside the diff), fall back to a summary-only
+        # round so no finding is silently lost.
+        findings = parse_findings(output)
+        output = FINDING_BLOCK_RE.sub("", output).strip()
+        summary = banner + output.rstrip() + "\n"
+        if findings and post_inline_review(self.pr, self.head_sha, findings):
+            summary += (
+                f"\n---\n📋 {len(findings)} finding(s) posted as inline review "
+                "comments on the diff; this comment carries the verdict and "
+                "state only.\n"
+            )
+        self.comment(summary)
+
+        if verdict_pass:
+            subprocess.run(
+                ["gh", "pr", "edit", str(self.pr), "--add-label", AI_REVIEW_PASSED_LABEL],
+                check=True,
+            )
+
+    def _knowledge_base_map(self) -> str:
+        """One-line summaries of every checklist entry, for progressive
+        disclosure: the agent reads the full file only when the PR touches
+        that area."""
+        lines = []
+        kb_dir = os.path.join(self.workspace, ".github", "agent-review")
+        for root, _dirs, files in os.walk(kb_dir):
+            for name in sorted(files):
+                if not name.endswith(".md") or name in (
+                    "instructions.md",
+                    "README.md",
+                    "prompt_template.md",
+                ):
+                    continue
+                path = os.path.join(root, name)
+                rel = os.path.relpath(path, self.workspace)
+                with open(path) as f:
+                    entry_ids = re.findall(r"^-\s+`([\w-]+#\w[\w-]*)`", f.read(), re.M)
+                ids = ", ".join(f"`{i}`" for i in entry_ids)
+                if ids:
+                    lines.append(f"- `{rel}` — rules with IDs: {ids}")
+                else:
+                    # orientation files carry no citable rule IDs; hint at
+                    # when reading them pays off
+                    hint = (
+                        "orientation map — read when the diff touches modules you cannot place"
+                        if "/context/" in rel.replace(os.sep, "/")
+                        else "maintenance doc, no rules"
+                    )
+                    lines.append(f"- `{rel}` — {hint}")
+        return "\n".join(lines)
+
+    def _waived_findings(self) -> list[str]:
+        """path:line of inline findings a reviewer has waived."""
+        waived = []
+        for c in self._review_comments():
+            body = c.get("body", "")
+            if c.get("in_reply_to_id") or INLINE_MARKER not in body:
+                continue
+            if not body.startswith(WAIVED_PREFIX):
+                continue
+            waived.append(f"`{c.get('path')}:{c.get('line')}`")
+        return waived
+
+    def _touched_domains(self) -> list[dict]:
+        registry_path = os.path.join(self.workspace, ".github", "agent-review", "domains.yaml")
+        files = self._gh_json("pr", "view", str(self.pr), "--json", "files", "-q", "[.files[].path]")
+        with open(registry_path) as f:
+            return resolve_domains(f.read(), files)
+
+    def _last_agent_comment_text(self) -> str:
+        comments = self._gh_json("pr", "view", str(self.pr), "--json", "comments", "-q", ".comments")
+        for c in reversed(comments):
+            if BOT_MARKER in c.get("body", ""):
+                return c.get("body", "")
+        return ""
+
+    def post_notice(self, text: str, new_state: State | None = None):
+        body = f"<!-- {BOT_MARKER} -->\n{text}"
+        if new_state is not None:
+            body += "\n\n" + new_state.signature(self.head_sha)
+        self.comment(body)
+
+    # ---- event dispatch ---------------------------------------------------
+
+    def handle(self) -> int:
+        name, _, action = self.event.partition("/")
+        self.head_sha = self._gh("pr", "view", str(self.pr), "--json", "headRefOid", "-q", ".headRefOid")
+
+        if name == "pull_request_target":
+            return self._handle_pr_event(action)
+        if name == "issue_comment":
+            return self._handle_comment()
+        if name == "pull_request_review_comment":
+            return self._handle_review_comment()
+        return 0
+
+    def _handle_pr_event(self, action: str) -> int:
+        labels = self._gh_json(
+            "pr",
+            "view",
+            str(self.pr),
+            "--json",
+            "labels",
+            "-q",
+            "[.labels[].name]",
+        )
+
+        if action == "labeled":
+            # The event payload does not tell us WHICH label; re-fetch the
+            # latest label timeline. If our label is gone, the label was not
+            # the one we care about.
+            if AI_REVIEW_LABEL not in labels:
+                return 0
+            if not self.actor_can_write():
+                print(f"actor {self.actor} lacks write access; ignoring", flush=True)
+                return 0
+            if not self.author_in_allowlist():
+                self.post_notice(
+                    "AI review POC 未覆盖此 PR（作者不在灰度名单），已忽略并移除标签。如需参与请在 RFC #21451 留言。",
+                )
+                subprocess.run(
+                    ["gh", "pr", "edit", str(self.pr), "--remove-label", AI_REVIEW_LABEL],
+                    check=False,
+                )
+                return 0
+            self.run_agent_round(round_no=1)
+            return 0
+
+        if action == "unlabeled":
+            # We cannot see which label was removed from `labels`; if the
+            # ai-review label is no longer present, treat as a stop request
+            # only when the previous state was active.
+            if AI_REVIEW_LABEL in labels:
+                return 0
+            if self.state.state in ("reviewing", "waiting-human", "passed"):
+                subprocess.run(
+                    ["gh", "pr", "edit", str(self.pr), "--remove-label", AI_REVIEW_PASSED_LABEL],
+                    check=False,
+                )
+                self.post_notice(
+                    "🛑 AI review 已被终止（label 被移除）。如需重新开始，请重新打 `ai-review` 标签。",
+                    new_state=State(state="stopped", round=self.state.round, total=self.state.total),
+                )
+            return 0
+
+        if action == "synchronize":
+            if AI_REVIEW_LABEL not in labels:
+                return 0
+            if self.state.state == "stopped":
+                return 0
+            if self.state.state == "passed":
+                subprocess.run(
+                    ["gh", "pr", "edit", str(self.pr), "--remove-label", AI_REVIEW_PASSED_LABEL],
+                    check=False,
+                )
+            if self.state.total >= MAX_TOTAL_ROUNDS:
+                self.post_notice(
+                    f"AI review 已达到整个 PR 的轮次预算上限（{MAX_TOTAL_ROUNDS} 轮），"
+                    "暂停响应。reviewer 可重新打 `ai-review` 标签重置预算。",
+                )
+                return 0
+            self.run_agent_round(round_no=1)
+            return 0
+
+        return 0
+
+    def _handle_comment(self) -> int:
+        body = self.comment_body or ""
+        if not body or self.state.state == "stopped":
+            return 0
+
+        # Reviewer stop command.
+        if STOP_RE.search(body):
+            if not self.actor_can_write():
+                print(f"actor {self.actor} lacks write access; ignoring stop", flush=True)
+                return 0
+            self.post_notice(
+                "🛑 AI review 已被终止。如需重新开始，请重新打 `ai-review` 标签。",
+                new_state=State(state="stopped", round=self.state.round, total=self.state.total),
+            )
+            return 0
+
+        # Reviewer waiver: top-level /ai-review-waive waives ALL open
+        # findings, then triggers one re-evaluation round (it costs agent
+        # compute, so it counts against the budget).
+        if WAIVE_RE.search(body):
+            if not self.actor_can_write():
+                print(f"actor {self.actor} lacks write access; ignoring waive", flush=True)
+                return 0
+            return self._waive_all()
+
+        # Only an explicit slash command counts as addressing the agent.
+        if not MENTION_RE.search(body):
+            return 0
+        if self.state.state in ("passed", "none"):
+            self.post_notice(
+                "AI review 已结束。如需重新评审，请让 reviewer 重新打 `ai-review` 标签。",
+            )
+            return 0
+        if self.state.total >= MAX_TOTAL_ROUNDS:
+            self.post_notice(
+                f"AI review 已达到整个 PR 的轮次预算上限（{MAX_TOTAL_ROUNDS} 轮），暂停响应。",
+            )
+            return 0
+
+        next_round = self.state.round + 1
+        closing = next_round > MAX_ROUNDS_PER_PUSH
+        self.run_agent_round(round_no=next_round, closing=closing)
+        return 0
+
+    # ---- waivers and inline threads ---------------------------------------
+
+    def _review_comments(self) -> list[dict]:
+        return self._gh_json("api", f"repos/:owner/:repo/pulls/{self.pr}/comments?per_page=100")
+
+    def _edit_review_comment(self, comment_id: int, body: str):
+        self._gh_json(
+            "api",
+            f"repos/:owner/:repo/pulls/{self.pr}/comments/{comment_id}",
+            "-X",
+            "PATCH",
+            "-f",
+            f"body={body}",
+        )
+
+    def _thread_root(self, comment: dict) -> dict | None:
+        """Follow in_reply_to_id to the root comment of a thread (bounded)."""
+        root = comment
+        for _ in range(10):
+            if root.get("in_reply_to_id") is None:
+                return root
+            root = self._gh_json("api", f"repos/:owner/:repo/pulls/{self.pr}/comments/{root['in_reply_to_id']}")
+        return None
+
+    def _waive_comment(self, comment: dict) -> bool:
+        """Prefix one inline finding comment with the waived banner."""
+        body = comment.get("body", "")
+        if INLINE_MARKER not in body or body.startswith(WAIVED_PREFIX):
+            return False
+        self._edit_review_comment(comment["id"], f"{WAIVED_PREFIX} by @{self.actor}]**\n\n{body}")
+        return True
+
+    def _waive_all(self) -> int:
+        roots = [
+            c
+            for c in self._review_comments()
+            if INLINE_MARKER in c.get("body", "")
+            and not c.get("in_reply_to_id")
+            and not c.get("body", "").startswith(WAIVED_PREFIX)
+        ]
+        for c in roots:
+            self._waive_comment(c)
+        self.post_notice(
+            f"⚖️ @{self.actor} waived all {len(roots)} open finding(s). "
+            "Re-evaluating: waived findings will not count toward MUST-FIX."
+        )
+        if self.state.state in ("reviewing", "waiting-human"):
+            if self.state.total >= MAX_TOTAL_ROUNDS:
+                return 0
+            next_round = self.state.round + 1
+            closing = next_round > MAX_ROUNDS_PER_PUSH
+            self.run_agent_round(round_no=next_round, closing=closing)
+        return 0
+
+    def _handle_review_comment(self) -> int:
+        """Replies inside an inline finding thread: `/ai-review-waive` waives
+        that single finding; `/ai-review` triggers the next round. Replies to
+        threads the agent did not start are ignored."""
+        body = self.comment_body or ""
+        if not body:
+            return 0
+        comments = {c["id"]: c for c in self._review_comments()}
+        ours = [c for c in comments.values() if INLINE_MARKER in c.get("body", "")]
+        if not ours:
+            return 0
+        # the event's comment itself
+        event_comment = comments.get(self._event_comment_id)
+        if not event_comment:
+            return 0
+        root = self._thread_root(event_comment)
+        if not root or INLINE_MARKER not in root.get("body", ""):
+            return 0
+
+        if WAIVE_RE.search(body):
+            if not self.actor_can_write():
+                print(f"actor {self.actor} lacks write access; ignoring waive", flush=True)
+                return 0
+            if self._waive_comment(root):
+                self.post_notice(
+                    f"⚖️ @{self.actor} waived the finding at `{root.get('path')}:"
+                    f"{root.get('line')}`. It will not count toward MUST-FIX."
+                )
+            return 0
+
+        if MENTION_RE.search(body):
+            if self.state.state in ("passed", "none", "stopped"):
+                return 0
+            if self.state.total >= MAX_TOTAL_ROUNDS:
+                self.post_notice(
+                    f"AI review 已达到整个 PR 的轮次预算上限（{MAX_TOTAL_ROUNDS} 轮），暂停响应。",
+                )
+                return 0
+            next_round = self.state.round + 1
+            closing = next_round > MAX_ROUNDS_PER_PUSH
+            self.run_agent_round(round_no=next_round, closing=closing)
+        return 0
+
+
+def main() -> int:
+    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
+    parser.add_argument("--comment-body-file", default="")
+    parser.add_argument("--comment-id", type=int, default=0)
+    parser.add_argument("--workspace", default=".")
+    parser.add_argument("--pr", type=int, required=True)
+    parser.add_argument("--event", required=True)
+    parser.add_argument("--actor", default="")
+    args = parser.parse_args()
+
+    comment_body = ""
+    if args.comment_body_file and os.path.exists(args.comment_body_file):
+        with open(args.comment_body_file) as f:

+# AI Code Review
+
+The AI review agent provides deep, on-demand code review for pull requests. It complements — never replaces — human review: first-pass screening (CODEOWNERS routing, gemini-code-assist comments) and CI run automatically on every PR, while the AI review agent handles the deep rounds that a reviewer explicitly requests. The agent can never approve or merge; its verdict is advisory input for the human reviewer.
+
+The mechanism was proposed in [RFC #21451](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/issues/21451) and is currently in a **gray release** (limited authors, opt-in per PR).
+
+## How it works, end to end
+
+```text
+reviewer applies "ai-review" label
+        │
+        ▼
+workflow gate (write permission + author in allowlist)
+        │
+        ▼
+orchestrator assembles prompt ──► dsh agent (headless) ──► findings
+        │                                                      │
+        ▼                                                      ▼
+state restored from last                  one COMMENT-level review with
+agent comment (signature block)           inline comments on code lines
+        │                                                      │
+        ▼                                                      ▼
+        └────────────── summary comment (verdict + signature) ──┘
+        │
+        ▼
+multi-round: author replies with /ai-review ──► next round
+new push ──► ai-review-passed revoked ──► incremental re-review
+```
+
+### Triggering and the gray-release gate
+
+- A reviewer with write permission applies the `ai-review` label to a PR.
+- The PR author must be listed in `.github/agent-review/allowlist.txt`. For any other PR the agent posts a single notice and removes the label. The gray release scales by editing this file; removing lines rolls it back with no code change.
+- During the gray release the agent's PR comments are posted by the maintainer's bot account, with an "AI review" banner marking them as machine output and clarifying that `ai-review-passed` is not an approve.
+
+### Review rounds
+
+Each round is one agent invocation. The orchestrator assembles the prompt deterministically:
+
+1. the output protocol (finding format, severities, verdict marker),
+2. a working-environment section (where the PR code, docs and guidelines live),
+3. a knowledge-base map — file paths plus rule IDs, not full contents,
+4. the list of knowledge-base domains the PR touches (resolved from `domains.yaml`),
+5. the PR diff, the agent's previous comment, and the author's reply.
+
+The agent reads the referenced checklist files itself from the checked-out repository and cites only rules it has actually read (every finding must carry a `file:line`, a rule ID and a severity — findings without grounding are invalid).
+
+### Multi-round interaction and termination
+
+State is carried in a machine-readable signature block at the end of every agent comment, so nothing needs to be stored outside GitHub:
+
+```text
+<!-- ai-review: state=reviewing | round=2/5 | total=6 | head=abc123 -->
+```
+
+| Event | Effect |
+|---|---|
+| Author replies with the `/ai-review` command | next round (plain comments, CI bots and human conversations are ignored) |
+| Author pushes a commit | `ai-review-passed` revoked, round budget reset, incremental re-review of the new diff |
+| Reviewer comments `/ai-review-waive` on a PR comment | ALL open findings waived (marked on the inline comments), one re-evaluation round runs |
+| Reviewer replies `/ai-review-waive` inside one finding's thread | that single finding is waived |
+| Reviewer removes the label or comments `/ai-review-stop` | agent stops; a newer trigger always cancels the in-flight round (latest wins) |
+| All MUST-FIX resolved | agent emits `AI-REVIEW-VERDICT: PASS`; the orchestrator applies `ai-review-passed` |
+| Round cap reached (5 per push) | closing summary, state `waiting-human`, a human decides |
+| Whole-PR budget exhausted (15 rounds) | agent goes silent until a reviewer re-applies the label |
+
+`ai-review-passed` is **not an approve**. The agent posts issue comments and COMMENT-level reviews only — it has no permission to approve, merge or push, and human review remains the merge gate.
+
+## For PR authors
+
+1. Ask a maintainer to add you to the allowlist (or self-request in RFC #21451).
+2. When you want a deep review, ask a reviewer to apply the `ai-review` label to your PR.
+3. The agent posts findings as inline comments on your diff plus one summary comment. To trigger the next round, add a **top-level PR comment** containing `/ai-review` — replies inside an inline finding thread also reach the agent, but a plain comment without the command never does.
+4. Fix what is marked `MUST-FIX` and push. The agent re-reviews the new diff automatically; when nothing blocking remains it applies the `ai-review-passed` label and a human reviewer takes over.
+5. Everything is optional: without the label your PR flow is unchanged.
+
+## Knowledge base maintenance
+
+The review rules live in `.github/agent-review/` and follow the project's ownership model — the people who own a module own the review rules for it:
+
+```text
+.github/agent-review/
+├── instructions.md        # output protocol (maintainers)
+├── allowlist.txt          # gray-release authors (maintainers)
+├── domains.yaml           # coarse path-glob → domain registry (maintainers)
+├── L1/checklist.md        # cross-domain global rules (maintainers)
+└── L2/<domain>/           # one directory per domain, owned by that
+    └── checklist.md       #   domain's CODEOWNERS owners
+```
+
+- **Ownership is enforced by CODEOWNERS.** Each `L2/<domain>/` directory gets one CODEOWNERS entry naming that domain's owners (later entries win over the `/.github` wildcard). Editing a domain's rules then requires those owners' approval — the same gate as editing the code itself.
+- **Updating rules** is an ordinary PR against the checklist file. Changes are effective for the next review round; there is no deployment step.
+- **Adding a domain** takes three steps: create `L2/<domain>/checklist.md` with stable rule IDs (`L2-<domain>#slug`), add a coarse glob entry to `domains.yaml`, append the CODEOWNERS entry. Keep domains coarse — per-file directories are explicitly avoided.
+- **Rule discipline**: rule IDs are stable API (findings cite them); every rule must be decidable from the diff and repository files (things needing test runs or hardware belong to human review); explicitly exclude what the agent should not report.
+
+During the gray release, maintainer feedback on the agent's inline comments (agree/disagree/corrections) is the main input for checklist iteration. Collect it and land checklist updates in small weekly batches rather than one change per finding.
+
+## Components
+
+| Path | Role |
+|---|---|
+| `.github/workflows/ai_review.yml` | trigger orchestration (label / comment / push), gates, agent job on the self-hosted CPU pool |
+| `.github/workflows/scripts/ai_review.py` | state machine, prompt assembly, finding parsing, inline-review posting |
+| `.github/workflows/dockerfiles/Dockerfile.ai-review` | preinstalled agent image (Node + dsh CLI), rebuilt manually |
+| `.github/workflows/_schedule_ai_review_image_build.yaml` | image build workflow (manual/deliberate, no schedule) |
+| `.github/agent-review/` | instructions, knowledge base, allowlist, domain registry |
+
+The agent engine is deliberately decoupled: the orchestrator invokes a configurable command (a repository variable), so the underlying engine can be replaced without workflow surgery.

[Doc] Keep commit messages brief and report validation details in PRs (#22618)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

Keep commit history readable and give reviewers one place to find the
evidence for an inference change. The contribution guide asks for a
brief problem statement, fix, and validation outcome in the commit body.

The PR template collects detailed accuracy and performance results under
**How was this patch tested?**, following the [upstream vLLM
template](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md).
It asks for matched baseline and PR results, dataset and metric for
accuracy, and hardware, P/D topology, token lengths, and concurrency for
serving benchmarks. Authors identify which chip and deployment
combinations they measured when describing an optimization shared across
A3 and A5.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

No. The change affects contributor documentation and the PR template.

### How was this patch tested?

- `markdownlint-cli@0.45.0` passed on `AGENTS.md` and the contribution
guide. `git diff --check` passed.
- Rendered the guide and PR template. Verified the guide links resolve,
the template headings are preserved, and the new prompts are inside the
testing section's author instructions.
- Local `bash format.sh ci` stopped during Windows hook setup because
nodeenv could not parse the Node.js prerelease version.
- Model accuracy and serving benchmarks are inapplicable to this
documentation change.

---

### Checklist

#### Testing

- [ ] **Boundary / edge-case coverage**: I reviewed whether this change
involves
boundary conditions (e.g. empty input, single/zero element, min/max
values,
off-by-one, sequence-length limits, integer overflow). Where applicable,
I
added unit tests covering these edge cases in `tests/ut/` or
`tests/e2e/`.
- [ ] **Regression test**: If this PR fixes a bug, I added a regression
test
  that would fail without the fix.
- [ ] **Error / failure path coverage**: I covered abnormal paths
(exceptions,
timeouts, out-of-range, division by zero) in addition to the happy path.
- [ ] **Meaningful & reliable tests**: New tests assert real behavior
and are
  not written merely to satisfy CI.
- [ ] **Performance impact**: If this PR touches a performance-sensitive
path,
  I attached benchmark results and added performance regression tests.

[Feature][Model] Support prefill context parallelism for Qwen3.8-Flash-Next (#21693)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

Enable prefill context parallelism (PCP) for Qwen3.8-Flash-Next on Model
Runner V2. Reuse the KDA projection sharding over TP × PCP for Gated
DeltaNet and process each rank's heads in global causal token order.
Share `pcp_gather_tokens` and `pcp_scatter_tokens`, including the
fixed-size index buffers, across Kimi KDA, Qwen GDN, and PLE. Follow the
GLM KPool layout for QSA by gathering cache inputs in global request
order and computing TopK with rank-local queries. PLE keeps
segment-specific n-gram history. The PCP manager supplies its existing
token mappings. The QSA cache builders use the corresponding upstream
interfaces for vLLM main and v0.33.0.

The model-level checks require DCP=1 and GDN key/value head counts
divisible by TP × PCP. The upstream GDN internal checkpoint path retains
its dispatch conditions.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes. With Model Runner V2, `--prefill-context-parallel-size` enables the
Qwen3.8-Flash-Next PCP path. The model support matrix marks PCP as
unverified for A2/A3 and 950DT.

### How was this patch tested?

- **Earlier NPU revision.** Ascend A3, W8A8, TP8, DP1, DCP1, expert
parallelism, vLLM main, eager, CANN 9.2.1 with the matching 9.3.0
transformer operator and OPP. Compared PCP=1 and PCP=2 at temperature 0
with 24 generated tokens. All tokens matched for the 2,053-token and
4,101-token single prompts and the long prompt in a mixed batch. Both
short continuations matched the first two tokens and then diverged. The
controlled one-word answer and the next token for a fixed prefix
matched.
- **Focused CPU coverage.** Added or updated tests for PCP token
ordering and empty ranks, QSA cache owners and global writes, PLE
segment history, and GDN head sharding and chunk handling. The earlier
paired-main run across the five affected unit-test files reported 146
passed and four failures, all four reproduced on the unchanged base. The
focused QSA and GDN chunk subset reported 14 passed.
- **After rebase.** The five isolated QSA CPU cases passed on each
upstream interface. A CPU check covered 16 combinations of the GDN fused
prefill dispatch conditions. Ruff lint, Ruff formatting, and `git diff
--check` passed.
- **Local hook checks.** The commit-range run passed Ruff, codespell,
typos, Markdown lint and the Python source checks. The logger,
long-function and symbolic-shape checks passed when invoked directly.
The Windows runner could not complete the actionlint and Gitleaks hooks.
GitHub CI covers those checks.
- **Shared PCP operators (`4669bed98`).** Ruff lint and formatting,
codespell, typos, Markdown lint, the Python package and import checks,
and `git diff --check` passed. Isolated CPU checks covered fixed-size
token reordering and padding, Torch custom-op registration and fake
shapes, and the two QSA forward signatures with mocked collectives.
Repository pytest was blocked by missing `uvloop` in the local CPU
environment. The full local hook run stopped while setting up
actionlint.
- **QSA decode graph follow-up (`9886b2ba0`).** Capture records the PCP
cache gather. Replay uses fixed local query and global write sizes, and
updates the restore indices in the captured buffer. All 74 local QSA
FIA/GBSA dispatch tests passed. Isolated CPU checks covered ranks with
zero, one, and two live tokens on paired main and v0.33.0rc0, and
verified the shared restore buffer address on main. Ruff lint and
formatting, codespell, typos, Markdown lint, and `git diff --check`
passed. Repository pytest remains blocked by missing `uvloop`, and the
full hook run stopped during actionlint setup.
- **Remaining validation.** NPU capture and replay for QSA
`FULL_DECODE_ONLY`, the PCP=1 versus PCP=2 comparison on both vLLM
interfaces, the 32-question AISBench GPQA Diamond run, and performance
measurements are pending.

[CI] Right-size CPU runners for lightweight control-plane jobs (#22476)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

Most control-plane CI jobs — test selection, matrix setup, benchmark
artifact merging, release packaging, and slash-command handling — spend
their run time on GitHub API calls and file I/O rather than CPU. Running
them on 8- or 4-core self-hosted runners wastes capacity that
compilation, unit-test, and pre-commit jobs actually need. This PR
right-sizes those jobs across three steps, keeping run logic unchanged
except for runner labels and the dispatch consolidation:
1. Downsize CPU runners for lightweight jobs
- 8-core → 2-core: nightly/weekly setup-vars and
merge-benchmark-artifacts, select-all-tests, upload-merged-new-tests
(release code packaging), and the a3/a3-560t setup steps
- 8-core → 4-core: doc translation, full-test selection
- 4-core → 2-core: PR command handlers (/cancel, /rerun, /run, /e2e,
/revert, /cherry-pick), fork coverage comment, upstream tag resolution,
doctest planning, multi-arch image manifest merge jobs (manifest push
only, no compilation), and the profiling plan step
Jobs that genuinely need their cores stay unchanged: pre-commit with
mypy and its cache warm-up (8-core), the cpu-ut partition running
tests/ut (8-core), csrc cache builds and profile trace parsing
(16-core), and docker builds (4-core).
2. Consolidate /nightly dispatch jobs into one matrix job — the ten
dispatch-* jobs become a single matrix job whose legs are composed by
authorize, so only selected targets start a runner (2-core,
max-parallel: 2). Run links travel via dispatch-link-* artifacts, and a
noop leg preserves the previous all-skip behavior while still letting
post-links report the command result.
3. Move pure I/O bot jobs to 1-core runners — gate comment/refresh,
issue triage, merge-conflict check, PR close, e2e result reporting,
refresh-ci-gate relay, recipe preview comments, matrix/setup and
parse-trigger steps, stale management, and slash-command dispatch now
run on linux-amd64-cpu-1-hk.
New runner labels (linux-amd64-cpu-1-hk, linux-aarch64-cpu-2) are
registered in .github/actionlint.yaml so the CI lint hook passes.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

No. This is a CI/infrastructure-only change; runtime and user-facing
behavior are unaffected.

### How was this patch tested?

- actionlint (runner-label lint hook)
- CI workflow runs exercised on the new linux-amd64-cpu-1-hk /
linux-aarch64-cpu-2 labels

---

### Checklist

#### Testing

- [ ] **Boundary / edge-case coverage**: I reviewed whether this change
involves
boundary conditions (e.g. empty input, single/zero element, min/max
values,
off-by-one, sequence-length limits, integer overflow). Where applicable,
I
added unit tests covering these edge cases in `tests/ut/` or
`tests/e2e/`.
- [ ] **Regression test**: If this PR fixes a bug, I added a regression
test
  that would fail without the fix.
- [ ] **Error / failure path coverage**: I covered abnormal paths
(exceptions,
timeouts, out-of-range, division by zero) in addition to the happy path.
- [ ] **Meaningful & reliable tests**: New tests assert real behavior
and are
  not written merely to satisfy CI.
- [ ] **Performance impact**: If this PR touches a performance-sensitive
path,
  I attached benchmark results and added performance regression tests.

[CI] Unify agent workflow credentials with the AI review job (#22654)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

The agent jobs in this repository (doc auto-translate and main2main)
currently carry their own per-workflow model credentials
(`DEEPSEEK_API_KEY` / `MAIN2MAIN_API_KEY`). The AI review job introduced
by #22319 already defines a dedicated credential pair (`AI_REVIEW_KEY` /
`AI_REVIEW_API`) for the same DeepSeek channel.

This PR points doc translation and main2main at that shared pair, so the
repository configures one credential set for all agent jobs instead of
duplicating keys per workflow:

- **doc translate** (`schedule_doc_translate.yaml`, `po_translate.py`):
- the job reads the key from `AI_REVIEW_KEY` and the endpoint from
`AI_REVIEW_API` (falling back to `https://api.deepseek.com`);
- `po_translate.py` gains `--api-key` / `--base-url` with the env
fallback chain `TRANSLATE_API_KEY` -> `AI_REVIEW_KEY` ->
`DEEPSEEK_API_KEY` (the old var kept as a last-resort fallback);
- `normalize_model()` accepts both the CLI form `deepseek/<model>` and
the raw HTTP model id `<model>`; the per-run `model` workflow_dispatch
input is kept, and the chosen model is logged and recorded in the
auto-translate PR body.
- **main2main** (`schedule_main2main.yaml`):
- `AI_REVIEW_KEY` is exported as `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY`, which the built-in
`deepseek` provider of `opencode` reads directly (default endpoint
`https://api.deepseek.com`, the same channel), so the generated
`auth.json` is no longer needed;
- the default model is `deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash`, and the provider
catalog is extended with that id because models.dev does not list it yet
(same pattern the workflow already used for `deepseek-flash`).

Once #22319 configures `AI_REVIEW_KEY` / `AI_REVIEW_API` in the repo
settings, no additional secret or variable is required by these
workflows; `TRANSLATE_MODEL` remains an optional variable to override
the scheduled translation model. The old `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY` /
`MAIN2MAIN_API_KEY` secrets are no longer referenced and can be removed
after both workflows pass.

Note: this PR should be merged after the `AI_REVIEW_KEY` /
`AI_REVIEW_API` secrets from #22319 are configured; until then the two
workflows have no valid credential to run with.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

### How was this patch tested?

---

### Checklist

#### Testing

- [ ] **Boundary / edge-case coverage**: I reviewed whether this change
involves
boundary conditions (e.g. empty input, single/zero element, min/max
values,
off-by-one, sequence-length limits, integer overflow). Where applicable,
I
added unit tests covering these edge cases in `tests/ut/` or
`tests/e2e/`.
- [ ] **Regression test**: If this PR fixes a bug, I added a regression
test
  that would fail without the fix.
- [ ] **Error / failure path coverage**: I covered abnormal paths
(exceptions,
timeouts, out-of-range, division by zero) in addition to the happy path.
- [ ] **Meaningful & reliable tests**: New tests assert real behavior
and are
  not written merely to satisfy CI.
- [ ] **Performance impact**: If this PR touches a performance-sensitive
path,

[BugFix][PCP] Use rank-local target batches for DFlash and DSpark profiling (#22656)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

DFlash and DSpark consume a full target context for draft KV
precomputation. With target PCP enabled, using the global token budget
for target startup profiling also inflates the prefill MC2/MegaMoE
capacity on each rank. This can reduce the headroom available for the KV
cache.

- Follow up on #21985 by reusing its per-rank budget for the target and
prefill MoE capacity.
- Gather the full dummy context in the existing DFlash and DSpark
proposal paths. For example, a global budget of 16,384 tokens with
PCP=8, DCP=1, 64 requests, three speculative tokens, and eager execution
yields a 2,400-token target dummy budget. The draft still receives
16,384 context rows, and target sampling uses the local batch.
- Run Kimi K3 and GLM-5 draft context projections during profiling
before KV cache allocation.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes. Startup memory reservations and the resulting KV cache budget can
change when DFlash or DSpark is used with PCP.

### How was this patch tested?

- **Source-isolated CPU regression suite** — 92 cases passed after
rebasing onto upstream main. Coverage includes the target and MC2
budget, draft-only gathering and truncation, PCP=1, non-profile paths,
collective failure propagation, local target sampling, and context
projection before allocation. Device communication and model forwards
were mocked.
- **Static checks** — Ruff lint and format checks and `git diff --check`
passed.
- The regular pytest entry point stopped while loading
`tests/ut/conftest.py` because the local CPU environment lacks
`cpuinfo`.
- The manual pre-commit run was interrupted while installing the
`actionlint` hook environment.
- **NPU validation pending.** Compare startup peak HBM and final KV
cache capacity on the same DFlash and DSpark PCP configurations, then
run a serving smoke test.

---

### Checklist

#### Testing

- [x] **Boundary / edge-case coverage**
- [x] **Regression test**
- [x] **Error / failure path coverage**
- [x] **Meaningful & reliable tests**
- [ ] **Performance impact** — NPU memory comparison pending.

[BugFix][CI] Fix silent checkout failure when nightly dispatches with a branch ref (#22903)

## What this PR does / why we need it?

Manually dispatched multi-node nightlies die silently when
`vllm_ascend_ref` is a branch name (e.g. the workflow default `main`).

In `checkout_src()` the script runs under `set -euo pipefail` and
resolves the ref against PR refs:

```bash
PR_REF=$(git ls-remote origin 'refs/pull/*/head' | grep "^${VLLM_ASCEND_REF}" | awk '{print $2}' | head -1)
```

When the ref is `main`, `grep` matches nothing in the `refs/pull/*/head`
list, exits 1, and `pipefail` + `set -e` terminate the whole script
immediately after `git clone --recurse-submodules` finishes - with no
error output. Any workflow_dispatch run with `request_id` set (making
`is_pr_test=true`, so `checkout_src` is entered) and the default ref
fails in Stream logs within ~3.5 minutes; every other matrix job in the
same run is skipped.

Evidence (run
[45109329614](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/actions/runs/45109329614),
dispatched with `vllm_ascend_ref=main`): both
`MiniMax-M3-w8a8-PP-prefix-PD` and `DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-w4a8-PD-MRV2`
jobs died 2s after the googletest submodule checkout (04:04:49 ->
04:04:51) with `run.sh exited with code 1`, before installing
dependencies or launching any test. No container/infra failure involved
- pods were ready and the clone succeeded.

The `/nightly` command path is unaffected because it dispatches with the
PR head SHA, which grep does match - which is why this latent bug
(introduced by #17848) went unnoticed for scheduled nightlies: they do
not set `request_id` and never enter `checkout_src`.

Fix: append `|| true` so the no-match case becomes an empty `PR_REF`
that falls through to the intended `else` branch (`git checkout main`).
Behavior is unchanged for PR-head SHA refs.

## Related issues

None.

## Test cases passed

- Local reproduction with the extracted pipeline: ref=`main` now yields
an empty `PR_REF` (script survives, falls to branch checkout);
ref=`<sha>` still resolves the matching PR ref.
- `bash -n` syntax check passes on the modified script.

- vLLM main:
https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/c410543d9ffff03f5f6c4a8c0ae1d3ad082c4a15

Signed-off-by: CuixyHW <cuixuanyu1@huawei.com>

@@ -289,7 +289,12 @@ checkout_src() {
         echo "Cloning vllm-ascend from $VLLM_ASCEND_REMOTE_URL"
         git clone --depth 1 --recurse-submodules "$VLLM_ASCEND_REMOTE_URL" "$WORKSPACE/vllm-ascend"
         cd "$WORKSPACE/vllm-ascend"
-        PR_REF=$(git ls-remote origin 'refs/pull/*/head' | grep "^${VLLM_ASCEND_REF}" | awk '{print $2}' | head -1)
+        # Under `set -euo pipefail` grep exits 1 when VLLM_ASCEND_REF is a
+        # branch name (e.g. main) that matches no refs/pull/*/head entry,
+        # which silently killed the whole script right after cloning. Add
+        # `|| true` so "no PR ref matched" falls through to the branch

[Performance] Fuse the mamba align block-table gather into one Triton kernel on Ascend (#21196)

## Description

Port of vLLM #58737 to vllm-ascend.

`mamba_get_block_table_tensor`'s "align" branch takes the last `1 +
num_speculative_blocks` block-table entries of each request. As PyTorch
ops this expands to **seven eager kernel launches over a `(num_reqs,)`
tensor** - one element per op at one-request decode - so the cost is
launch overhead, not work. Both Ascend call sites (the GDN attention
metadata builder, run by every Qwen3.8 / Qwen3-Next GDN model each step,
and the GLM RecoverSSM metadata builder) are host-side builders
executing **every step, outside any captured graph**, at any batch size.

The upstream kernel cannot be inherited: vLLM gates it with `if not
block_table.is_cuda`, so NPU always falls back to the seven-op
expression **regardless of the vLLM version**. This PR ships the same
kernel for triton-ascend (NPU-only) and swaps the two call sites.
Equivalence vs the expression was probed bit-exact (8/8 shapes) before
implementation; the outputs are integer block IDs (exact-compare
category), so model-level outputs are unchanged by construction.

## Performance

### 910B probe (triton-ascend 3.6.0, per call)

Device ~370 -> ~215 us (**-42%**), host ~247 -> ~121 us (**-51%**); flat
across 1..512 rows - the win is per-launch, per-step.

### E2E on 910B (Qwen3.8-27B-w8a8, MTP5, TP4)

Arms = base tree vs this PR, alternating with cold restarts. Concurrency
1, five independent pairs, zero flips, B faster in all: ITL **-0.112 /
-0.168 / -0.245 ms (-0.7 / -1.0 / -1.4%)**; aisbench TPOT 17.3 -> 17.1
ms, E2E latency -1.0%. Concurrency 8: mean -0.3 .. -1.5%. The -0.112 ms
c1 delta reproduces exactly on an older stack (D05-17U); UT gate 89/89
on the bench NPU; zero failed requests across all rounds.

### Op-level A/B on 910C (both call sites)

A3 single node; arms = `main` (`3e9e1869a`) vs same tree + this patch;
`--profiler-config` torch profiler (CANN `ascend_pt`), per-kernel device
time aggregated from the rank-0 profile. Kernel counts are exact
multiples of the decode step count, so the op-level comparison is
deterministic.

*Qwen3.8-27B-w8a8 - default config (TP4, no spec decode, prefix caching
on -> `align`); the GDN build calls the helper exactly 3x per decode
step, 10 launches per call:*

| | baseline (7-op expression) | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| kernel launches / decode step | 30 | 3 (**-90%**) |
| family device time, 1022-step window | ~59.8 ms | 3.92 ms (**-93.4%**)
|
| kernel mean time | ~1.9 us | **1.28 us** |
| E2E ITL, 1 req x 1024 tok | 17.093 ms | 16.952 ms (**-0.141 ms /
-0.83%**) |

*GLM-5.3-Flash-w8a8 - `--use-replayssm --mamba-backend triton` (TP8,
MTP3), the only config selecting call site 2; RecoverSSM rebuilds 3x per
step:*

| | baseline | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| kernel launches / decode step | ~21 | 3 (**-86%**) |
| family device time, 273-step window | ~16.3 ms | 1.04 ms (**-94%**) |
| E2E ITL | 36.657 ms | 36.503 ms (**-0.154 ms / -0.42%**) |

Net decode-step saving is ~0.14 ms on both models (device ~55 us + host
~85 us from 27 / 18 removed launches), fully accounting for the measured
ITL deltas within ~3%. The absolute per-step saving is
batch-size-independent (fixed 3 builder calls/step, ~1.3 us kernel), so
the relative gain peaks at low concurrency. Scoping: under the V2
runner, default GLM serving (no `--use-replayssm`) leaves both call
sites dormant - the host build is bypassed by the in-graph
fused-metadata path (verified: no A/B difference); GLM numbers above are
RecoverSSM-specific, Qwen numbers need nothing beyond default prefix
caching.

### Load-bearing details kept from upstream

- `block_table_stride_0: tl.int64` - without it `req_idx * stride`
computes in i32 and wraps past 2^31 elements; the `torch.gather` it
replaces indexes in 64-bit.
- `do_not_specialize_on_alignment` on all three pointers - callers pass
row-sliced views (`block_table[:num_reqs]`); without it a misaligned
slice JIT-recompiles mid-step. Verified on triton-ascend 3.6.0.
- `n_out` / `block_size` are session-constant and alignment
specialization is suppressed, so the kernel compiles exactly once per
process; no variants remain, so JIT warmup registration does not apply.

## What's Changed

- new `vllm_ascend/ops/triton/mamba/align_block_table.py`: kernel
(verbatim port incl. both annotations) + `mamba_get_block_table_tensor`
wrapper mirroring upstream's contract (`none` passthrough, num_reqs
derived from the block table, asserted equal to seq_lens rows).
NPU-only.
- `ops/gdn_attn_builder.py`: import swap; the `[:num_reqs]` slice is now
unconditional (the Ascend wrapper asserts row equality on all vLLM
versions; the old version-gated slice would trip the assert on 0.32.0).
- `models/glm5next/recoverssm_metadata.py`: import swap.
- tests: `tests/ut/ops/test_mamba_align_block_table.py` keeps the `none`
passthrough + shared builders; on-device equivalence moved to
`tests/e2e/nightly/single_node/ops/singlecard_ops/triton/test_mamba_align_block_table.py`;
align-mode cases of the pre-existing builder UTs
(`test_gdn_attn_builder.py`, `test_glm5next_recoverssm_metadata.py`)
gated on NPU availability.

## Test

`tests/ut` runs on CPU runners, so it covers only the CPU-reachable
behavior; the on-device matrix (request counts, block sizes, speculative
depths, non-contiguous block_table, row-sliced views, seq_len-0 clamp,
empty batch; `rtol=0, atol=0`) lives in the e2e nightly test and passed
**89/89 on 910B** before the reorganization.

Possible follow-up (out of scope): generalize the upstream `is_cuda`
gate so device-triton backends inherit the fused path directly.

- vLLM main:
https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/c410543d9ffff03f5f6c4a8c0ae1d3ad082c4a15

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM Ascend project
+"""CPU-reachable tests for the Ascend fused mamba "align" block-table gather.
+
+Port of vLLM's ``tests/v1/attention/test_mamba_align_block_table.py`` for
+``vllm_ascend.ops.triton.mamba.align_block_table``. ``tests/ut`` runs on CPU
+runners (``tests/ut/conftest.py`` pins ``torch.npu.is_available()`` to False
+there), and the "align" branch launches the fused NPU Triton kernel, so the
+only behavior reachable here is the ``"none"`` passthrough. The on-device
+kernel equivalence runs live in
+``tests/e2e/nightly/single_node/ops/singlecard_ops/triton/test_mamba_align_block_table.py``,
+which imports this module's builders the way ``test_gdn_prepare.py`` reuses
+``tests/ut/ops/test_gdn_attn_builder.py``.
+"""
+
+import torch
+from vllm.v1.kv_cache_interface import MambaSpec
+
+from vllm_ascend.ops.triton.mamba.align_block_table import (
+    mamba_get_block_table_tensor,
+)
+
+WIDTH = 64
+
+
+def _spec(block_size: int, num_speculative_blocks: int) -> MambaSpec:
+    # Only block_size and num_speculative_blocks are read by the align branch;
+    # shapes/dtypes just have to be well formed for the frozen dataclass.
+    return MambaSpec(
+        block_size=block_size,
+        shapes=((1,),),
+        dtypes=(torch.float32,),
+        num_speculative_blocks=num_speculative_blocks,
+    )
+
+
+def _reference(block_table, seq_lens, block_size, num_spec_blocks):
+    """The align branch exactly as it was before the fusion."""
+    start_indices = (seq_lens - 1) // block_size
+    start_indices = start_indices.clamp(min=0)
+    offsets = torch.arange(1 + num_spec_blocks, device=block_table.device, dtype=torch.int32)
+    indices_to_gather = (start_indices.unsqueeze(1) + offsets).to(torch.int64)
+    return torch.gather(block_table, 1, indices_to_gather)
+
+
+def _make(nreq, block_size, nspec, device, noncontig=False):
+    torch.manual_seed(0)
+    width = WIDTH * 2 if noncontig else WIDTH
+    bt = torch.randint(0, 5000, (nreq, width), dtype=torch.int32, device=device)
+    if noncontig:
+        # Every other column: stride(1) == 2, which a kernel assuming a unit
+        # column stride would read straight through, silently returning the
+        # wrong blocks.
+        bt = bt[:, ::2]
+        assert not bt.is_contiguous()
+    # Keep start + nspec inside the row, which the gather already requires.
+    hi = max(1, (WIDTH - 1 - nspec) * block_size)
+    sl = torch.randint(0, hi, (nreq,), dtype=torch.int32, device=device)
+    return bt, sl
+
+
+def test_cpu_none_mode_passes_through():
+    bt = torch.arange(12, dtype=torch.int32).reshape(3, 4)
+    sl = torch.tensor([1, 2, 3], dtype=torch.int32)
+    assert mamba_get_block_table_tensor(bt, sl, _spec(16, 3), "none") is bt

+# mamba_align_block_table
+
+## Description
+
+- **Location**: [`mamba/align_block_table.py`](../mamba/align_block_table.py).
+  `mamba_get_block_table_tensor` is the Python entry point for the private
+  `_mamba_align_block_table_kernel` Triton kernel.
+- **Function**: In `mamba_cache_mode="align"`, return the trailing
+  `1 + num_speculative_blocks` physical state-block IDs of every request from
+  the full position-indexed mamba block table, so the downstream state kernels
+  know which physical blocks to read and write for speculative-decode
+  alignment. One launch replaces the seven-op torch expression the upstream
+  expression expands to.
+- **Formula**: For request `i`, `start_i = max((seq_lens[i] - 1) //
+  block_size, 0)` and `out[i, j] = block_table[i, start_i + j]` for
+  `j` in `[0, 1 + num_speculative_blocks)`.
+- **Algorithm flow** (processed row by row, independently): one program per
+  request; `BLOCK = next_power_of_2(n_out)` lanes with a mask gather
+  `n_out` consecutive entries starting at the request's anchor column.
+- **Supported modes**: align-mode mamba/GDN/KDA state caches on Ascend NPU
+  (A2/A3 verified). Called from host-side attention metadata builders
+  (`ops/gdn_attn_builder.py`, `models/glm5next/recoverssm_metadata.py`)
+  every step, outside any captured graph. `"none"` mode returns the block
+  table unchanged. The kernel path requires NPU tensors.
+- **Compilation**: `block_size` and `n_out` are session-constant, so the
+  kernel compiles once per process. `do_not_specialize_on_alignment` on all
+  three pointers keeps row-sliced caller views from JIT-recompiling mid-serve.
+
+## Parameters
+
+The wrapper allocates and returns `out`; all other arguments are inputs.
+
+| Parameter | Input/Output/Attribute | Description | Data type | Data format |
+| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
+| `block_table` | Input | Full position-indexed mamba state block table, `[R, cdiv(max_model_len, block_size)]` | INT32 | 2D, strided |
+| `seq_lens` | Input | Current sequence lengths, `[R]` | INT32 | 1D, strided |
+| `kv_cache_spec` | Attribute | `MambaSpec` providing `block_size` and `num_speculative_blocks` | `MambaSpec` | N/A |
+| `mamba_cache_mode` | Attribute | `"align"` takes the kernel; `"none"` returns `block_table` unchanged | `str` | N/A |
+| `out` (return) | Output | Trailing-window physical block IDs, `[R, 1 + num_speculative_blocks]` | INT32 | Contiguous 2D, freshly allocated |
+
+## Constraints
+
+- `seq_lens` and `block_table` must have the same row count `R` and reside on
+  the same device (asserted).
+- The kernel path requires NPU tensors. The align-mode cases of the builder
+  unit tests are gated on NPU availability (`tests/ut` runners have none).
+- `block_table` may be a row-sliced view (`block_table[:num_reqs]`); both
+  strides are honored, including a column stride other than 1.
+- `block_table_stride_0` is annotated `tl.int64`: without it the row-offset
+  product wraps in i32 once a row offset reaches `2^31` elements, a limit the
+  `torch.gather` it replaces does not have.
+- `R == 0` returns an empty `[0, n_out]` tensor without launching a `(0,)`
+  grid. Zero-length requests clamp to row 0. Reads past the request's used
+  blocks but inside the row are legal and return unused entries, exactly as
+  the replaced expression did.
+- The output is bit-exact with the seven-op expression (`atol=0, rtol=0`).
+
+## Origin and Differences
+
+- **Origin**: Port of vLLM [#58737](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/58737)'s
+  CUDA fused kernel; replaces the "align" branch of vLLM's
+  `mamba_get_block_table_tensor`, which on NPU always expanded to seven eager
+  kernel launches because upstream gates the fused path with `is_cuda`.
+- **Differences**:
+    - Built for triton-ascend; keeps both load-bearing annotations from
+      upstream (`tl.int64` row stride, `do_not_specialize_on_alignment`).
+    - NPU-only: vllm-ascend runs on NPU, so no non-NPU fallback is carried;
+      the align-mode builder unit-test cases skip on CPU runners instead.
+    - The wrapper derives `num_reqs` from the block table and asserts row and
+      device equality, mirroring the upstream contract.
+
+## Test Cases
+
+Per the repo test organization, `tests/ut` runs on CPU runners, so the split is:
+
+- `tests/ut/ops/test_mamba_align_block_table.py` — the `"none"` passthrough
+  (the only CPU-reachable behavior); hosts the shared builders (`_spec`,
+  `_reference`, `_make`).
+
+  ```bash
+  pytest -sv tests/ut/ops/test_mamba_align_block_table.py
+  ```
+
+- `tests/e2e/nightly/single_node/ops/singlecard_ops/triton/test_mamba_align_block_table.py`
+  — on-device kernel equivalence with `rtol=0, atol=0`: parametrized request
+  counts, block sizes and speculative depths, a non-contiguous block table
+  (column stride 2), row-sliced views, the `seq_len == 0` clamp and the empty
+  batch, reusing the UT's builders.
+
+  ```bash
+  pytest -sv tests/e2e/nightly/single_node/ops/singlecard_ops/triton/test_mamba_align_block_table.py
+  ```
+
+Probe and engine-level performance measurements are recorded in
+[PR #21196](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/pull/21196).

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM Ascend project
+"""Fused mamba "align" block-table gather on Ascend (port of vLLM #58737).
+
+``mamba_get_block_table_tensor``'s "align" branch takes the last
+``1 + num_speculative_blocks`` block-table entries of each request. As PyTorch
+ops this is seven kernel launches over a ``(num_reqs,)`` tensor -- a single
+element in a one-request decode -- so almost all of its cost is launch
+overhead rather than work. On 910B the seven eager ops measure ~370 us device
+/ ~247 us host per call while one fused Triton kernel takes ~215 us / ~121 us
+(-42% device, -51% host), flat across batch sizes.
+
+The fused kernel cannot be inherited from upstream: vLLM gates it with
+``if not block_table.is_cuda``, so NPU always falls back to the seven-op torch
+expression regardless of the vLLM version. This module ships the same kernel
+for triton-ascend and mirrors upstream's semantics (num_reqs derived from
+the block table, asserted equal to the seq_lens rows).
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import torch
+from vllm.triton_utils import tl, triton
+from vllm.v1.kv_cache_interface import KVCacheSpec, MambaSpec
+
+
+@triton.jit(do_not_specialize_on_alignment=["out_ptr", "block_table_ptr", "seq_lens_ptr"])
+def _mamba_align_block_table_kernel(
+    out_ptr,
+    block_table_ptr,
+    block_table_stride_0: tl.int64,
+    block_table_stride_1,
+    seq_lens_ptr,
+    seq_lens_stride,
+    block_size,
+    n_out,
+    BLOCK: tl.constexpr,
+):
+    """Gather the last ``n_out`` block-table entries of each request.
+
+    One program per request; both strides are passed explicitly because
+    callers may hold non-contiguous views of the block table. The two
+    annotations above are load-bearing: ``block_table_stride_0: tl.int64``
+    keeps the row-offset product from wrapping past 2**31 elements, and the
+    pointer alignment de-specialization keeps row-sliced views from
+    recompiling mid-serve.
+    """
+    req_idx = tl.program_id(0)
+    seq_len = tl.load(seq_lens_ptr + req_idx * seq_lens_stride)
+    # A zero-length request in a graph has an invalid block table; clamp
+    # to 0 so it reads a valid row, exactly as the previous clamp_ did.
+    start = tl.maximum((seq_len - 1) // block_size, 0)
+    offs = tl.arange(0, BLOCK)
+    mask = offs < n_out
+    vals = tl.load(
+        block_table_ptr + req_idx * block_table_stride_0 + (start + offs) * block_table_stride_1,
+        mask=mask,
+        other=0,
+    )
+    # `out` is freshly allocated by the caller and therefore contiguous, so its
+    # row stride is exactly n_out.
+    tl.store(out_ptr + req_idx * n_out + offs, vals, mask=mask)
+
+
+def mamba_get_block_table_tensor(
+    block_table: torch.Tensor,
+    seq_lens: torch.Tensor,
+    kv_cache_spec: KVCacheSpec,
+    mamba_cache_mode: str,
+) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """Ascend counterpart of vLLM's ``mamba_get_block_table_tensor``.
+
+    Identical contract, except the fused Triton kernel is taken on NPU (the
+    upstream kernel is CUDA-gated).
+    """
+    if mamba_cache_mode == "none":
+        return block_table
+    assert isinstance(kv_cache_spec, MambaSpec)
+    num_reqs = block_table.shape[0]
+    n_out = 1 + kv_cache_spec.num_speculative_blocks
+    assert seq_lens.shape[0] == num_reqs, f"seq_lens has {seq_lens.shape[0]} rows, block_table has {num_reqs}"
+    assert seq_lens.device == block_table.device, (
+        f"seq_lens is on {seq_lens.device}, block_table on {block_table.device}"
+    )
+    out = block_table.new_empty((num_reqs, n_out))
+    if num_reqs == 0:
+        return out
+    _mamba_align_block_table_kernel[(num_reqs,)](
+        out,
+        block_table,
+        block_table.stride(0),
+        block_table.stride(1),
+        seq_lens,
+        seq_lens.stride(0),
+        kv_cache_spec.block_size,
+        n_out,
+        BLOCK=triton.next_power_of_2(n_out),
+    )
+    return out

## What this PR does / why we need it?

Adds the shared KV-pool A/B hit-watch harness and the three A3 four-card
e2e cases that are already green and need no product-code changes:

- P1: DSV4-Flash TP4+EP, MTP1, mooncake block-key layerwise
(`four_card/test_deepseek_v4.py`)
- P5: DSV4-Flash DSpark PP2xTP2, mooncake non-layerwise
(`four_card/model_runner_v2/test_spec_pp_accuracy.py`)
- P6: DSV4-Flash DSA-PCP MTP TP2xPCP2+EP, memcache non-layerwise
(`four_card/context_parallel/pool/test_deepseek_v4_pool.py`)

`get_metrics` / `get_acceptance` helpers in `tests/e2e/conftest.py`, and
the matching `estimated_times.yaml` entries.

P3/P10/P11 and the product fixes they still need stay in the main
pool-watch PR; this PR is test-only so it can merge first.

No. Tests only.

CI testing only. Triggered `/e2e` for the three test files on both pins;
