[Performance][MoE] Avoid redundant token ID preprocessing before hash TopK (#21452)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

Remove redundant per-layer INT64 casts and padding normalization before
native sqrt-softplus Hash TopK routing. The active native kernel already
accepts INT32/INT64 IDs and maps `-1` to token zero on load. Keep
preprocessing in the PyTorch vision route, which performs its own
indexing. Communication, padding and sequence-parallel row alignment
remain intact.

Update the existing router unit tests and nightly operator test to cover
raw padding IDs and both ID dtypes, and include the performance
release-note fragment. These are the four changed files in this PR.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Lower hash-routing overhead without new configuration or API changes.
Routing outputs and padding/vision-sentinel semantics are preserved.

### How was this patch tested?

**Current head `94286f914`:** scope reduced to the router, existing
unit/nightly tests and release note. Runtime code and the retained test
logic are unchanged from the previously tested head. Ruff check/format
passed for all three retained Python files; PR diff whitespace checks
and committed LF checks passed for all four remaining files. Fresh CI on
this head is pending. Local framework tests were not run because
PyTorch/vLLM/pytest are unavailable in the Windows checkout; earlier
full formatting attempts were blocked by Go/actionlint environment
setup.

**Previous CI evidence:** [run
44702245525](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/actions/runs/44702245525)
on `cc6314d89` passed 35 checks, including both CPU matrices and
selected NPU/upstream tests, with 14 configured skips. The only
remaining gate failure was missing CODEOWNERS approvals. These results
precede the current scope reduction.

**Recorded manual A5 evidence (one-off validation, not an additional
checked-in suite):** Ascend950DT_9582, CANN 9.3.0, PyTorch 2.10.0+cpu,
torch_npu 2.10.0.post7. A fresh single-op package from `fa7b6ff83`,
using the existing ABI-compatible binding, passed eight raw-ID cases in
1.22s: INT32/INT64, FP32/BF16 and eager/graph. Expert IDs matched
token-zero table rows, and raw/normalized IDs produced identical IDs and
weights. Strict library-map checks selected the fresh op-api/tiling
libraries with no old op-api library loaded. The compiler include trace
selects the common regbase header, which already normalizes padding.
This establishes the tested packaged A5 path, not execution of the
separate `arch35/` header. That header is unchanged in this PR. See the
[review
clarification](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/pull/21452#discussion_r4640041992).

**Prior A3 hardware evidence:**

**Real NPU execution:** Ascend910_9362 (A3), PyTorch 2.10.0, torch_npu
2.10.0.post4.dev20260715, FP32 router logits `[tokens, 384]`, TopK=6.

- 30 cases across tokens `{1, 23, 96, 132, 432}`, INT32/INT64 IDs, text
hash routing, mixed vision/hash routing and vision routing without a
hash table. Eager execution and NPU graph replay passed. Expert IDs and
weights are bit-identical between the original preprocessing path and
direct raw-ID input. Maximum FP32 weight error against an independent
CPU reference: `1.1920928955078125e-07` (rtol/atol `1e-5`; expert IDs
exact).
- 16 additional checked-in operator cases passed: FP32/BF16 logits,
INT32/INT64 IDs, hash/no-hash, eager/graph, raw padding IDs and image
sentinels. Expert IDs exact; weight tolerances `1e-5` for FP32 and
`1e-2` for BF16.
- Profiling four calls per path: baseline has four occurrences each of
Cast/Equal/Fill/Where plus four Hash TopK kernels; candidate contains
only four Hash TopK kernels.

**Paired NPU graph timings** (microseconds per ID-preprocessing + Hash
TopK chain, excluding router GEMM): 32 calls per graph, 10 replays per
sample, six samples with alternating A/B order; medians below.
Compilation, capture and profiling are outside the timed interval.

| Token rows | Original | Direct IDs | Reduction |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | 6.747 us | 3.609 us | 46.5% |
| 23 | 11.652 us | 6.003 us | 48.5% |
| 96 | 13.272 us | 9.199 us | 30.7% |
| 132 | 15.479 us | 9.791 us | 36.7% |
| 432 | 20.148 us | 14.505 us | 28.0% |

Hardware validation used the isolated Hash TopK package and binding from
`21609b11ee574c477e5f36c925921e2355df160c`, because the available image
ships an older extension ABI. The native kernel headers, Hash TopK
binding function, affected sqrt-softplus router branch and updated NPU
test source are identical to this main-branch port (base `1e2557aeb`).
The 16 operator test functions were executed directly against the real
isolated NPU binding; kernel outputs were not mocked.
Reproduce the retained regression coverage on a matching built runtime:

```bash
pytest -q tests/ut/ops/test_fused_moe.py -k 'hash_router or vision_router'
pytest -q tests/e2e/nightly/single_node/ops/singlecard_ops/test_moe_gating_top_k_hash.py
```

### Pre-PR review

Reuses existing native sentinel handling and removes temporary per-token
preprocessing tensors. No new runtime configuration, C++ operator
implementation, dependencies, persistent state, timeout or fallback
mechanism. The retained tests check raw-ID forwarding and real operator
outputs. Historical operator-chain measurements use bounded
shapes/replays and do not establish full-model throughput or multi-rank
acceptance. Fresh CI and owner approval remain required for the current
head.

### Checklist

- [x] Boundary/regression coverage: raw `-1`, both ID dtypes, vision
sentinels and sequence-parallel alignment.
- [x] Meaningful unit and nightly operator coverage.
- [x] Prior hardware/performance evidence reported with its scope and
limitations.
- [ ] Fresh CI on the current head.
- [ ] Required CODEOWNERS approvals.

[BugFix][MoE] Share DSpark MegaMoE contexts across CANN buffer APIs (#21727)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

DeepSeek V4.1 with DSpark and CANN MegaMoE creates separate target and
draft buffers on the same MC2 group. On A5, the second native context
can contain zero peer-buffer addresses, causing MegaMoE to fail during
startup profiling.

Keep one target-owned allocation on the MC2 group coordinator and give
the draft an independent metadata view over the same context and context
manager. Validate communication settings and capacity before sharing.
Identify MRv2 eager drafts by logical expert counts, including redundant
experts.

Bind CANN capacity queries by parameter name to support both the legacy
interface and the current interface with `intermediate_hidden`,
`combine_comm_mode`, and topology-dependent `server_num`. This updates
the approach in #20234 for current main and CANN 9.2.1 while preserving
main's buffer-sizing policy. Target and draft calls remain serialized.

During wake-up, the first stale model view rebinds the group-owned CANN
context and runs a barrier. Target and draft both refresh their own
runtime metadata from that context. The packaged MLA stream-lifetime
change is tracked in #22592.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Fixes conflicting MegaMoE communication contexts for DeepSeek V4.1
DSpark on A5. No additional configuration is required. Includes a
release note fragment.

### How was this patch tested?

- Focused CPU regression and lifecycle tests: **17 passed** with Python
3.12, torch 2.10.0, and vLLM `24420b7a341af37a9bc3186e6fc6062512e0aa58`:

  ```bash
TORCH_DEVICE_BACKEND_AUTOLOAD=0 VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=empty python3 -m
pytest -q \
    --confcutdir=tests/ut/ops \
    tests/ut/ops/test_mega_moe_context.py \
    tests/ut/ops/test_fused_mc2_sleep_state.py
  ```

- The deployment backport passed **26 CPU tests**, including
`test_moe_comm_method.py`.
- A smoke check against the installed CANN 9.2.1 native capacity-query
API passed for target 384 experts/top-k 6 and draft 128 experts/top-k 3
with P and D capacity settings. Each pair used one mocked allocation and
shared context identity.
- Ruff lint/format, codespell, typos, Python package initialization,
forbidden-import, and boolean-context checks passed.

- Review follow-up: **30 CPU unit tests passed** on Linux AArch64 with
Python 3.12.13, PyTorch `2.10.0+cpu`, pytest 8.4.2 and vLLM
`24420b7a341af37a9bc3186e6fc6062512e0aa58`. Ran `python3 -m pytest -q
-ra` on `test_mega_moe_context.py`, `test_moe_comm_method.py` and
`test_fused_mc2_sleep_state.py` with the repository CPU mocks. The new
sleep/wake-up case covers both target-first and draft-first recovery. A5
hardware coverage remains pending.

### Checklist

- [x] Boundary / edge-case coverage
- [x] Regression test
- [x] Error / failure path coverage
- [x] Meaningful & reliable tests

- vLLM main:
https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/c410543d9ffff03f5f6c4a8c0ae1d3ad082c4a15

+"""Regression coverage for target/draft sharing without native collectives."""

+import sys
+import unittest
+from inspect import signature

+    combine_quant_mode=0,
+    comm_alg="",
+    combine_comm_mode=0,
+    topk_weights_type=0,
+):
+    return SimpleNamespace(**locals(), context=object(), _ctx_manager=object(), ep_world_size=8, ccl_buffer_size=4096)
+
+
+def _legacy_size_query(
+    ep_world_size,
+    moe_expert_num,
+    num_max_tokens_per_rank,
+    num_topk,
+    hidden,
+    max_recv_token_num=0,
+    dispatch_quant_mode=0,
+    dispatch_quant_out_dtype=None,
+    combine_quant_mode=0,
+    comm_alg="",

+
+def _current_size_query(

+        self.size_patch = patch.object(

+"""Main-owned MegaMoe communication storage for serialized target/draft calls."""
+
+from collections.abc import Callable
+from importlib import import_module

+def is_draft_moe_config(moe_config: Any, vllm_config: Any) -> bool:
+    """Identify a draft communicator even when MRv2 constructs it under target config.
+
+    MRv2 eager DSpark forwards retain the target's context flag. The loaded
+    target/draft model descriptors still distinguish their logical expert
+    counts; redundant target slots must not turn a target into a draft.
+    """
+    model_config = vllm_config.model_config
+    if model_config is None:
+        raise RuntimeError("MegaMoe role detection requires a model config")
+    is_draft_runner = getattr(model_config, "runner_type", None) == "draft"
+    speculative = getattr(vllm_config, "speculative_config", None)
+    draft_config = getattr(speculative, "draft_model_config", None)
+    if draft_config is None:
+        return is_draft_runner
+    target_experts = int(model_config.get_num_experts())
+    draft_experts = int(draft_config.get_num_experts())
+    # Equal expert layouts already share a cached MoECommMethod, including
+    # its lazy initialization when it was last constructed by the draft.
+    if target_experts == draft_experts:
+        return False
+    logical_experts = int(moe_config.num_experts) - int(getattr(moe_config, "global_redundant_expert_num", 0))
+    return is_draft_runner or logical_experts == draft_experts
+
+
+def get_main_owned_buffer(
+    scope: Any,
+    factory: Callable,
+    *,
+    is_draft: bool,
+    recreate_on_wake: bool = False,
+    group: Any,
+    num_experts: int,
+    num_max_tokens_per_rank: int,
+    num_topk: int,
+    **kwargs,
+):
+    """Allocate once for main; give draft its own metadata over that storage.
+
+    The MC2 group coordinator owns the allocation for its lifetime. Target
+    and draft must execute serially. A draft-first request or insufficient
+    capacity fails before a second native communication context is created.
+    """
+    bound = signature(factory).bind(group, num_experts, num_max_tokens_per_rank, num_topk, **kwargs)
+    bound.apply_defaults()
+    params = bound.arguments
+    owner = getattr(scope, "_main_mega_moe_symm_buffer", None)
+    if owner is None:
+        if is_draft:
+            raise RuntimeError("Main must initialize MegaMoe before the draft")
+        owner = factory(*bound.args, **bound.kwargs)
+        if recreate_on_wake:
+            # Keep the target's allocation parameters even when the draft wakes first.
+            def recreate_for_group(new_group):
+                return factory(new_group, num_experts, num_max_tokens_per_rank, num_topk, **kwargs)
+
+            owner._recreate_for_group = recreate_for_group
+        scope._main_mega_moe_symm_buffer = owner
+        return owner
+
+    if group is not owner.group:
+        raise RuntimeError("Main and draft MegaMoe process groups differ")
+    missing = object()
+    for name in (
+        "hidden",
+        "dispatch_quant_mode",
+        "dispatch_quant_out_dtype",
+        "combine_quant_mode",
+        "comm_alg",
+        "combine_comm_mode",
+        "topk_weights_type",
+    ):
+        if name in params and params[name] != getattr(owner, name, missing):
+            raise RuntimeError(f"Incompatible shared MegaMoe setting: {name}")
+    if num_max_tokens_per_rank > owner.num_max_tokens_per_rank:
+        raise RuntimeError("Draft token capacity exceeds the main allocation")
+    module = import_module(factory.__module__)
+    # CANN added intermediate_hidden and combine_comm_mode to the size API.
+    # Bind by name so older and newer signatures cannot shift positional args.
+    size_query = module._get_mega_moe_ccl_buffer_size
+    query_parameters = signature(size_query).parameters
+    ep_world_size = getattr(owner, "ep_world_size", None)
+    if ep_world_size is None or ep_world_size <= 0:
+        raise RuntimeError("Shared MegaMoe requires a positive ep_world_size")
+    size_params = dict(params, ep_world_size=ep_world_size, moe_expert_num=num_experts)
+    if "server_num" in query_parameters and getattr(owner, "topo_type", 0) != 0:
+        ranks_per_server = getattr(owner, "rank_num_per_server", None)
+        if ranks_per_server is None or ranks_per_server <= 0 or ep_world_size % ranks_per_server:
+            raise RuntimeError("Shared MegaMoe requires a positive rank_num_per_server that divides ep_world_size")
+        size_params["server_num"] = ep_world_size // ranks_per_server
+    required = size_query(**{name: size_params[name] for name in query_parameters if name in size_params})
+    if required > owner.ccl_buffer_size:
+        raise RuntimeError(f"Requested MegaMoe capacity {required} exceeds main's {owner.ccl_buffer_size} bytes")
+    view = SimpleNamespace(**vars(owner))
+    for name, value in params.items():
+        setattr(view, name, value)
+    assert view.context is owner.context
+    assert view._ctx_manager is owner._ctx_manager
+    return view

[BugFix] Preserve the DeepSeek-V4.1 MoE cursor during bounded replay (#22420)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

On a single Ascend A5 node serving prefill and decode together,
DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash GSM8K accuracy rose from **75.22% to 97.38% (+22.16
percentage points)** with this fix. These are three-round means among
completed answers. Counting all scheduled questions, the correct-answer
share rose from **2,905/3,957 (73.41%) to 3,833/3,957 (96.87%)**.

With `fast_moe_cold_start`, each MoE dispatch advances the cursor in the
current forward context. Bounded replay creates a new context with a
cursor of zero, so in the captured Flash runs decoder layers 21–39 used
expert weights from layers 0–18. The fix seeds the replay context with
the outer context's current cursor so the tail continues at the correct
layer.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes. It fixes incorrect DeepSeek-V4.1 outputs under SWA bounded replay
with speculative decoding disabled. Existing serving configurations can
be retained.

### How was this patch tested?

- **CPU regression:** All eight replay context cases passed in an
isolated local CPU run and failed at the cursor assertion on the
unpatched base. The supplied validation at Ascend `b64139a5` reports 114
focused tests passed on each vLLM ref (`ba15685a` and `v0.33.0`).
- **A5 mixed deployment:** The supplied A/B used DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash on
16-card Ascend950PR nodes, 200-shot GSM8K, concurrency 512, and 1,319
questions per round. Both arms used the downstream vLLM 0.32 debug
runtime with the same inference settings and SWA index implementation,
on different physical nodes. Read timeouts were 96 and 21, respectively.
The first baseline round also used a different retry policy. Replay
traces showed the correct expert layers in all six fixed samples and the
wrong layers in all nine baseline samples.
- **Disaggregated P/D:** The supplied A5 run also confirmed correct
prefill expert selection after the fix and scored 3,849/3,957 on GSM8K
(97.27%).
- **Local checks:** `bash format.sh ci`, `git diff --check`, Python
syntax, and the CODEOWNERS coverage check passed. Scoped mypy passed for
Python 3.10–3.12. Full local mypy reported identical diagnostics on the
clean base and patched branch in the Mac environment.

### Checklist

#### Testing

- [x] **Boundary / edge-case coverage**: Compact and untrimmed replay,
with and without sequence parallelism.
- [x] **Regression test**: The replay cursor assertion fails before the
fix.
- [x] **Error / failure path coverage**: Context and mask restoration
are tested after an exception.
- [x] **Meaningful & reliable tests**: The regression checks cursor
continuity and outer context isolation.
- [ ] **Performance impact**: The fix copies one host-side integer. The
supplied A/B measures accuracy.

[BugFix] Exempt empty files from CODEOWNERS coverage check in CI sparse checkout (#22662)

## What this PR does / why we need it?

The CODEOWNERS gate job checks out only `.github/` (sparse) so a PR
cannot weaken the gate script or CODEOWNERS. `is_contentless_file`
relied on `os.path.getsize`, which raises `OSError` for every file
outside `.github/` in that working tree, so the zero-byte exemption for
empty `__init__.py` broke in CI: unowned empty `__init__.py` files were
reported as coverage warnings again (e.g. run
[44713215032](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/actions/runs/44713215032/job/136211945876)).

unnoticed.

--long HEAD`, which works regardless of working-tree sparsity because
`actions/checkout` fetches all blobs even for a sparse checkout. The
working-tree fallback is kept for callers without a git size map, so
partial local checkouts still report missing files as unowned.

No. CI-only: fewer false "file has no CODEOWNERS owner" warnings for
empty `__init__.py` in the gate job. No release note fragment (dev
tooling, invisible to wheel/Docker users).

sparse working tree exemption via git sizes, and PR-only paths missing
from the base-branch size map still being reported. Full suite: 58
passed locally.
- Manual: `check-coverage` locally exempts 0-byte
`vllm_ascend/attention/__init__.py` via the git size map while 6KB
`vllm_ascend/models/__init__.py` is still reported.
- CI testing only for the NPU side (no hardware involved in this change;
gate job behavior verified by CI).
- vLLM main:
https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/c410543d9ffff03f5f6c4a8c0ae1d3ad082c4a15

commits.message: [Performance] Fuse rotated Engram gate on A3 (#21660) Keep the FP32 rotation projection separate and fuse normalization, scoring, masking and residual addition with distinct scoring and residual inputs. Add parity and graph replay coverage, documentation and a release note draft. ### What this PR does / why we need it? Fuse the post-projection gate for rotated DeepSeek V4.1 Engram checkpoints on A3. Keep the rotation GEMM in FP32 and use distinct scoring and residual inputs, preserving the original residual basis. A5 unrotated gating and the reference fallback remain available. Merged upstream main at a969ef789. The hardware-profile conflict retains both A3 rotated gating and the upstream local Host VMM capability; the CPU capability-matrix expectation now includes rotated gating. The PR title now uses the required [Performance] tag. ### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change? Yes. Rotated Engram checkpoints use the fused normalization/scoring/masking/residual path on A3. No new configuration is required. Operator documentation and release_notes/fragments/21660.yaml are included. ### Test Result 精度 性能 ### How was this patch tested? Validation of b7641c13e on 2026-11-18: - Full-repository `pre-commit run ruff-check --all-files --hook-stage manual` and `pre-commit run ruff-format --all-files --hook-stage manual`: passed. `git diff --check`: passed. - Server 199.203.1.6, container `vllm_0.32_lvgang`, A3 logical device 0: 25 tests passed in 47.57 s from `tests/e2e/nightly/single_node/ops/singlecard_ops/triton/test_engram_gate.py`, including BF16/FP32, no/shared/per-block rotation, empty and strided inputs, masked residual preservation, and model dispatch with NPU graph replay. - `python3 -m pytest --confcutdir=tests/ut/device -q tests/ut/device/test_hardware_profile.py`: 20 passed in 3.84 s. - Hardware environment: PyTorch 2.10.0+cpu, torch-npu 2.10.0.post7, triton-ascend 3.6.0.post2, vLLM 0.32.0+empty, CANN 9.2.1 container image, npu-smi 26.1.1. - The exact PR snapshot was extracted into `/tmp/pr21660-b7641c13e`; the installed checkout and running services were preserved. NPU tests shared a device with an existing service with the user's authorization, so these are correctness results, not performance measurements. - The container's vLLM release is older than current main: normal UT/E2E collection fails on missing `vllm.models.step5` / `vllm.v1.core.kv_cache_planning`. The focused NPU launcher `/tmp/pr21660-focused.py` bypassed unrelated package initializers and global conftest, using the real PR kernel, common helper, model layer, and unchanged test file. This is operator and graph coverage, not full model/E2E validation. - `bash format.sh ci` was attempted locally and in the container. Local Windows nodeenv setup failed; container dependency installation did not complete and was stopped. The complete hook suite still needs CI confirmation. - Current upstream E2E does not trigger on pushes. Adding `ready-precise` was denied by GitHub (`AddLabelsToLabelable`); a maintainer must add that label or trigger `/run`. Model-level accuracy, performance benchmarks, and full CI remain pending. --- ### Checklist #### Testing - [x] **Boundary / edge-case coverage**: I reviewed whether this change involves boundary conditions (e.g. empty input, single/zero element, min/max values, off-by-one, sequence-length limits, integer overflow). Where applicable, I added unit tests covering these edge cases in `tests/ut/` or `tests/e2e/`. - [x] **Regression test**: If this PR fixes a bug, I added a regression test that would fail without the fix. - [x] **Error / failure path coverage**: I covered abnormal paths (exceptions, timeouts, out-of-range, division by zero) in addition to the happy path. - [x] **Meaningful & reliable tests**: New tests assert real behavior and are not written merely to satisfy CI. - [x] **Performance impact**: If this PR touches a performance-sensitive path, I attached benchmark results and added performance regression tests. - vLLM main: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/c410543d9ffff03f5f6c4a8c0ae1d3ad082c4a15 --------- Signed-off-by: lvvgang Signed-off-by: lvvgang Co-authored-by: lvvgang

+"""Gate parity, including distinct scoring/residual bases and strided inputs."""
+
+import pytest

+from vllm_ascend.device.device_config import get_ascend_device_type
+from vllm_ascend.device.hardware import AscendDeviceType

+from vllm_ascend.ops.triton.engram_gate import fused_engram_gate
+
+HC = 4
+ROTATION_BLOCK = 32
+EPS = 1e-6
+
+
+def reference(hidden, kv, qw, kw, mask, rotation):
+    # Independently express the reference; residual must stay in its original basis.
+    dim = hidden.shape[-1]
+    h = hidden.float()
+    if rotation is not None:
+        blocks = h.reshape(*h.shape[:-1], dim // ROTATION_BLOCK, ROTATION_BLOCK)
+        if rotation.ndim == 2:
+            h = (blocks @ rotation.T).reshape_as(h)
+        else:
+            h = (blocks.unsqueeze(-2) @ rotation.transpose(-1, -2)).squeeze(-2).reshape_as(h)
+    key = kv[:, : HC * dim].reshape(hidden.shape).float()
+    value = kv[:, HC * dim :].float()
+    scale = torch.rsqrt(h.square().mean(-1) + EPS) * torch.rsqrt(key.square().mean(-1) + EPS)
+    dot = (h * (qw.float() * kw.float()) * key).sum(-1) * scale * dim**-0.5
+    magnitude = dot.abs().clamp_min(1e-6).sqrt()
+    gate = torch.sigmoid(torch.where(torch.signbit(dot), -magnitude, magnitude))
+    gate = gate.masked_fill(~mask[:, None], 0)
+    return (hidden.float() + gate[..., None] * value[:, None, :]).to(hidden.dtype)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.skipif(
+    get_ascend_device_type() not in (AscendDeviceType.A3, AscendDeviceType.A5),
+    reason="Engram gate routes on A3 (rotated) and A5 (unrotated)",
+)

+@pytest.mark.parametrize("rotation_kind", ["none", "shared", "per_block"])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("dtype", [torch.bfloat16, torch.float32])
+def test_engram_gate(tokens, dim, rotation_kind, dtype):
+    torch.manual_seed(42)
+    # Token and branch strides are deliberately non-contiguous, channels are contiguous.
+    hidden = torch.randn(tokens * 2, HC * 2, dim, device="npu", dtype=dtype)[::2, ::2]
+    kv = torch.randn(tokens * 2, (HC + 1) * dim, device="npu", dtype=dtype)[::2]
+    qw = torch.randn(HC, dim * 2, device="npu", dtype=dtype)[:, ::2]
+    kw = torch.randn_like(qw)
+    mask = (torch.arange(tokens * 2, device="npu") % 3 != 0)[::2]
+    rotation = None
+    if rotation_kind != "none":
+        shape: tuple[int, ...] = (ROTATION_BLOCK, ROTATION_BLOCK)
+        if rotation_kind == "per_block":
+            shape = (dim // ROTATION_BLOCK, *shape)
+        rotation = torch.randn(shape, device="npu", dtype=torch.float32) / ROTATION_BLOCK**0.5
+    gate_hidden = None if rotation is None else restore_engram_hidden(hidden, rotation)
+    expected = reference(hidden, kv, qw, kw, mask, rotation)
+    actual = fused_engram_gate(hidden, kv, qw, kw, mask, EPS, gate_hidden=gate_hidden)
+    torch.npu.synchronize()
+    tolerance = 1e-2 if dtype == torch.bfloat16 else 1e-4
+    torch.testing.assert_close(actual, expected, atol=tolerance, rtol=tolerance)
+    torch.testing.assert_close(actual[~mask], hidden[~mask], atol=0, rtol=0)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.skipif(get_ascend_device_type() != AscendDeviceType.A3, reason="Rotated model gate routes on A3")
+def test_rotated_engram_model_graph_replay():
+    torch.manual_seed(7)
+    tokens, dim = 7, 5120
+    hidden = torch.randn(tokens, HC, dim, device="npu", dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+    kv = torch.randn(tokens, (HC + 1) * dim, device="npu", dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+    mask = torch.ones(tokens, device="npu", dtype=torch.bool)
+    rotation = torch.randn(ROTATION_BLOCK, ROTATION_BLOCK, device="npu") / ROTATION_BLOCK**0.5
+    # Exercise real model dispatch without constructing a checkpoint linear layer.
+    layer = AscendEngram.__new__(AscendEngram)
+    torch.nn.Module.__init__(layer)
+    layer.dim, layer.hc_mult, layer.eps = dim, HC, EPS
+    layer.wkv = torch.nn.Identity()
+    layer.q_weight = torch.nn.Parameter(torch.randn(HC, dim, device="npu", dtype=torch.bfloat16))
+    layer.k_weight = torch.nn.Parameter(torch.randn(HC, dim, device="npu", dtype=torch.bfloat16))
+    with torch.inference_mode():
+        for _ in range(3):
+            layer(hidden, kv, mask, rotation)
+        torch.npu.synchronize()
+        graph = torch.npu.NPUGraph()
+        with torch.npu.graph(graph):
+            actual = layer(hidden, kv, mask, rotation)
+        for scale in (0.0, -0.5, 2.0):
+            hidden.normal_().mul_(scale)
+            kv.normal_()
+            mask.copy_(torch.arange(tokens, device="npu") % 2 == 0)
+            graph.replay()
+            torch.npu.synchronize()
+            expected = reference(hidden, kv, layer.q_weight, layer.k_weight, mask, rotation)
+            torch.testing.assert_close(actual, expected, atol=1e-2, rtol=1e-2)
+            torch.testing.assert_close(actual[~mask], hidden[~mask], atol=0, rtol=0)

[Feature] Fuse GatingTopK with EPLB expert mapping (#21587)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

With ModelRunnerV2 EPLB, expert selection writes logical expert IDs
before a separate Map kernel reads them and produces physical IDs. This
change adds an optional `expert_replica_routing_table` input to
`moe_gating_top_k_hash`, allowing supported routes to map the final IDs
before they leave on-chip memory.

The router automatically selects fusion on supported A3/A5 hardware for
ungrouped `sqrtsoftplus` routing. It reuses the existing periodic EPLB
table, including the AllGather table when applicable, and skips the
subsequent standalone Map. Weights are computed using logical IDs before
the output IDs are mapped. The router inherits upstream
`_select_experts` unchanged. An internal `_use_gating_top_k_with_map`
switch is resolved once at the first routing call, after EPLB/capture
setup and using the actual hidden size. The existing Ascend mapping hook
only reads this fixed choice; it does not reset or consume per-call
state. `_can_fuse_gating_map` checks eligibility once, while
`_get_gating_map_table` reads the current ordinary/AllGather table on
every nonempty fused call. Missing tables raise instead of returning
unmapped IDs. The original parent-fallback condition is preserved;
eligibility is resolved for the fixed model routing configuration. The
router retains the existing nonempty-input expectation: the reviewed
ModelRunnerV2 target paths skip zero batches or provide dummy/padded
tokens before routing. This PR does not add standalone zero-row TopK
support. Model routing configuration, including logical-ID capture, must
be finalized before the first routing call and remain fixed during
serving; this change does not add a capture setter override or support
runtime reconfiguration. The mapping-hook check can be removed when
upstream provides a backend contract for already-mapped routing results.
The original TopK expert-count checks remain unchanged; there is no
additional 512-expert fusion limit.

Routes with a logical-ID capture callback or unsupported fusion
conditions retain the original flow. The optional table defaults to
`None`, preserving standalone TopK behavior. Python and compiled
operators must come from matching versions.

Scope is GatingTopK+Map only; Dispatch+Record, MegaMoE+Record and the
separate block-FP8 compatibility fix are not included.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes. On supported A3/A5 ModelRunnerV2 EPLB routes, fusion is enabled
automatically and removes a separate expert-mapping operator launch per
MoE layer. No new flag is needed; replica-selection behavior is
unchanged.

### How was this patch tested?

- **25 CPU tests passed (19 router + 6 factory/patch):** upstream
selection flow, table forwarding, output dtype, no duplicate mapping,
capture configured before routing, unsupported configurations/hardware,
missing-table errors, and ordinary/AllGather table replacement. Tests
also cover one-time initialization for enabled and disabled choices,
kernel failure/retry, parent fallback, supported/unsupported vision
paths, EPLB disabled. Kernel and communication calls are mocked in these
tests; they validate control flow, not NPU execution.
- **20 A3 single-NPU tests passed in 10.00s** using a fresh build of the
kernel source: Ascend 910_9382, CANN 9.2.0, PyTorch 2.10.0, torch_npu
2.10.0.post7. These earlier component results cover the unchanged
kernel. The final fixed-switch router refactor was validated by the 25
CPU tests above; NPU and end-to-end router validation have not been
rerun after that refactor.
- Exact physical-ID agreement against both standalone Triton Map and an
independent CPU table lookup; exact weight agreement with the same TopK
operator with Map disabled.
- FP32/FP16/BF16, eager and NPU graph replay, mixed replica counts,
shuffled nonidentity placement, and in-place table updates.
- Representative `(tokens, experts, hash)` cases: `(1, 384, false)`,
`(33, 513, true)`, `(1025, 2048, false)`.
- Real `npu_moe_init_routing_v2` counts and production Record-buffer
increments match CPU expectations for count/cumulative formats,
recording enabled/disabled, repeated accumulation, and a local expert
range. The production AllGather counting helper also matches masked CPU
counts. These are single-device component checks, not distributed
collective validation.
- The single-NPU test lives in
`tests/e2e/nightly/single_node/ops/singlecard_ops/`, which is already
included by the A3 and A5 nightly single-card operator jobs. The old
PR-only A3 runner mapping has been removed. The relocation preserves the
test content exactly; Python syntax and `git diff --check` passed. NPU
execution under the new nightly directory was not rerun for this
relocation; the local `bash format.sh ci` attempt could not run because
`pre-commit` is not installed.
- Ruff lint/format and `git diff --check` passed. The full local `bash
format.sh ci` attempt was blocked by CRLF shell-script line endings;
full repository CI remains pending.

Reproduction (with matching compiled operators and their environment
sourced):

```bash
python -m pytest tests/ut/ops/test_gating_map_router.py -q
python -m pytest tests/e2e/nightly/single_node/ops/singlecard_ops/test_gating_map_npu.py -q
```

Remaining before merge review:

- [ ] A5 hardware validation.
- [ ] Distributed and target-model validation of the final branch.
- [ ] Matched profiling and end-to-end performance evidence, reported
separately.
- [x] User-facing release note fragment added in
`release_notes/fragments/21587.yaml`.
- [ ] Full repository CI.

### Checklist

- [x] Boundary / edge-case coverage committed.
- [x] Regression and fallback coverage committed.
- [x] Correctness tests included in the PR.
- [ ] Performance evidence and regression coverage attached.

+
+
+def _map_inputs(rows, experts, dtype, with_hash=False):
+    generator = torch.Generator().manual_seed(42)
+    logits = torch.randn(rows, experts, generator=generator).to(dtype).npu()
+    bias = (torch.randn(experts, generator=generator) * 0.1).to(dtype).npu()
+    # Mixed replica counts and shuffled placement avoid an identity-map false positive.
+    counts = torch.arange(experts).remainder(3).add(1).int()
+    placement = torch.full((experts, 3), -1, dtype=torch.int64)
+    slots = torch.randperm(int(counts.sum()), generator=generator)
+    offset = 0
+    for expert, count in enumerate(counts.tolist()):
+        placement[expert, :count] = slots[offset : offset + count]
+        offset += count
+    table = build_expert_replica_routing_table(placement.npu(), counts.npu(), ep_rank=1)
+    kwargs = dict(x=logits, k=6, bias=bias, group_count=1, k_group=1, norm_type=2, renorm=0, routed_scaling_factor=1.5)
+    if with_hash:
+        kwargs.update(
+            input_ids=torch.arange(rows, device="npu").remainder(11),
+            tid2eid=torch.stack([torch.randperm(experts, generator=generator)[:6] for _ in range(11)]).int().npu(),
+        )
+    return kwargs, table, offset
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("rows,experts,with_hash", [(1, 384, False), (33, 513, True), (1025, 2048, False)])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("dtype", [torch.float32, torch.float16, torch.bfloat16])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("execution_mode", ["eager", "graph"])
+def test_gating_map_matches_separate_ops(rows, experts, with_hash, dtype, execution_mode):
+    kwargs, table, physical_experts = _map_inputs(rows, experts, dtype, with_hash)
+    op = torch.ops._C_ascend.moe_gating_top_k_hash
+    reference_weights, logical_ids, _ = op(**kwargs)
+    logical_cpu = logical_ids.cpu().long()
+    graph = None
+    if execution_mode == "graph":
+        for _ in range(3):
+            op(**kwargs, expert_replica_routing_table=table)
+        torch.npu.synchronize()
+        graph = torch.npu.NPUGraph()
+        with torch.npu.graph(graph):
+            weights, ids, _ = op(**kwargs, expert_replica_routing_table=table)
+    previous = None
+    for update in (False, True):
+        if update:
+            # Preserve addresses to catch stale tables during graph replay too.
+            table.copy_((table + 1).remainder(physical_experts))
+        if graph is None:
+            weights, ids, _ = op(**kwargs, expert_replica_routing_table=table)
+        else:
+            graph.replay()
+        expected = table.cpu()[torch.arange(rows)[:, None] % table.shape[0], logical_cpu]
+        separate = map_to_physical_for_ascend(logical_ids, table)
+        torch.testing.assert_close(separate.cpu(), expected, rtol=0, atol=0)
+        torch.testing.assert_close(ids.cpu(), expected, rtol=0, atol=0)
+        torch.testing.assert_close(weights, reference_weights, rtol=0, atol=0)
+        assert (expected.long() != logical_cpu).any()
+        if previous is not None:
+            assert (expected != previous).all()
+        previous = expected

[Doc][Recipe] Add Ascend overlay for MiniMax-M3.1-Flash (#22617)

### What this PR does / why we need it?
Add `recipes/overlays/MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3.1-Flash.yaml`, migrated from
`docs/source/tutorials/models/MiniMax-M3.1-Flash.md`, so recipes.vllm.ai
can
render the Ascend deployment lanes for this model on top of the upstream
base
recipe.

- Two Ascend variants: W8A8 (int8) on `ascend_910c` and W8A8 MXFP8 on
  `ascend_950dt_8x`. Both are ModelScope checkpoints served with
`--quantization ascend`, plus a DSpark speculative-decoding override
(seven
  draft tokens, eager draft, BF16 draft KV).
- Single-node presets: DP4 x TP4 / EP16 on Atlas 800I A3 and DP2 x TP4 /
EP8 on
  Atlas 950DT, FULL_DECODE_ONLY graphs, prefix caching.
- PD presets, selected by default for the `pd_cluster` strategy: A3
prefill
DP1 x TP4 x PP4 against a global DP8 x TP4 decode group over two hosts,
and
950DT prefill DP1 x TP4 x PP2 against a global DP4 x TP4 decode group.
Both
use the minimal multi-port external load balancer (one supervisor per
decode
host, `--data-parallel-multi-port-external-lb`) instead of the
tutorial's
per-rank `vllm serve` scripts, with MooncakeConnectorV2 on both pools
and
  the Ascend Router as the catalog's PD router.
- An `### Ascend deployment` guide section covering placeholders,
literal
ports, supervisor semantics, graph capture sizes, KV connector notes and
  startup order.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?
No. Recipes metadata only (builder output for Huawei hardware on
recipes.vllm.ai); no code, API, or runtime behaviour changes.

### How was this patch tested?
- `validate-source.mjs` (strict assemble + schema + JSON API build):
pass.
- `validate-ascend.mjs` repo-wide: 0 errors, 0 blocking; the two new PD
presets
only emit the optional ASC010 warning because no independent PD
expectation
  is supplied.
- Every rendered command was compared field by field against tutorial
sections
5.1 and 5.3: parallelism, dtypes, sequence limits, capture sizes,
environment,
  KV dtypes and pool shapes, ports, and tool-calling switches.
- The tutorial's PD launch (MooncakeConnectorV1, per-rank scripts) was
validated
on hardware. This overlay switches the launcher to the multi-port
external-LB
supervisor with MooncakeConnectorV2; that path was not run end-to-end on
NPU
  here, and the preset runbooks state it.

---

### Checklist

#### Testing

- [ ] **Boundary / edge-case coverage**: not applicable to a recipes
metadata
  change.
- [ ] **Regression test**: not applicable, this adds a new overlay.
- [ ] **Error / failure path coverage**: not applicable, no runtime
code.
- [ ] **Meaningful & reliable tests**: validation is by the recipes
renderer
  (strict assemble + schema) and by `validate-ascend.mjs`.
- [ ] **Performance impact**: none, documentation/metadata only.

- vLLM main:
https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/c410543d9ffff03f5f6c4a8c0ae1d3ad082c4a15

+# Source: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/9b088c6667cbb9cce3eaa5ad937548aad36e8e7e/recipes/models/MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3.1-Flash.yaml

+strategy_hardware:
+  # The tutorial documents a single-node split (A3: DP4 x TP4, 950DT: DP2 x TP4)
+  # and a 1P1D split (prefill TP4 x PP4/PP2, decode DEP over two hosts). The
+  # variants carry the common flags and every lane-specific flag lives in a
+  # preset, so the strategies that would re-size TP or add a second DP on top of
+  # the documented split are opted out:
+  #   - TEP/DEP single-node pin TP to the whole node and add their own DP
+  #     (TP16 on A3), and the multi-node TP/TEP variants spread one instance
+  #     across hosts instead of the tutorial's per-host DP ranks;
+  #   - multi_node_dep would size each host as a whole-node DEP pool, not the
+  #     tutorial's global DP8 (A3) / DP4 (950DT) group;
+  #   - single_node_tp is kept because the presets declare the extra DP flags;
+  #   - pd_cluster is enabled for the two qualified Huawei profiles only.
+  single_node_tep:
+    npu: unsupported
+  single_node_dep:
+    npu: unsupported
+  multi_node_tp:
+    npu: unsupported
+  multi_node_dep:
+    npu: unsupported
+  multi_node_tep:
+    npu: unsupported
+  pd_cluster:
+    npu: unsupported
+    ascend_910c: supported
+    ascend_950dt_8x: supported
+features:
+  spec_decoding:

+    # model, BF16 draft KV cache on both Ascend builds. Unlike the NVIDIA/AMD
+    # overrides there is no draft attention-backend field: the tutorial's
+    # validated command does not pass one.
+    hardware_overrides:
+      npu:
+        args:
+          - '--speculative-config'
+          - '{"method":"dspark","num_speculative_tokens":7,"enforce_eager":true,"kv_cache_dtype":"bfloat16"}'
+hardware_overrides:
+  npu:
+    extra_args:
+      - '--trust-remote-code'
+      # Both Ascend images ship no default executor backend for the documented
+      # DP/PP layouts.
+      - '--distributed-executor-backend'
+      - mp
+    extra_env:
+      VLLM_USE_MODELSCOPE: 'True'
+      VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER: '1'
+      PYTORCH_NPU_ALLOC_CONF: expandable_segments:True
+variants:
+  ascend_w8a8:
+    model_id: Eco-Tech/Minimax-M3.1-Flash-w8a8
+    label: W8A8 (ASCEND A3)
+    precision: int8
+    # The base recipe's AMD-only opt-ins (DBO/SP prefill, NVFP4 top-k, mono
+    # decode) have no Ascend path. Their modes are variant-filtered, so a new
+    # variant has to exclude them explicitly to stay renderable.
+    supported_features:
+      - tool_calling
+      - reasoning
+      - spec_decoding
+      - text_only
+    vram_minimum_gb: 514
+    description: >-
+      ModelSlim W8A8 build of the MiniMax M3.1-Flash checkpoint (~428B total /
+      23B active), served on one Atlas 800I A3 host with 16 x Ascend 910C
+      (64 GB). Requires --quantization ascend and the ModelScope repository.
+    supported_hardware:
+      - ascend_910c
+    tp:
+      ascend_910c: 4
+    extra_args:
+      - '--host'
+      - '0.0.0.0'
+      - '--served-model-name'
+      - minimax-m3.1-flash
+      - '--quantization'
+      - ascend
+      - '--max-model-len'
+      - '133000'
+      - '--enable-prefix-caching'
+    extra_env:
+      HCCL_OP_EXPANSION_MODE: AIV
+    install:
+      pip: false
+      docker:
+        command: "docker pull quay.io/ascend/vllm-ascend:minimax-m3.1-flash-a3-openeuler"
+    hardware_overrides:
+      ascend_910c:
+        docker_image: quay.io/ascend/vllm-ascend:minimax-m3.1-flash-a3-openeuler
+        docker_shm_size: 100g
+        docker_serve_command: "vllm serve"
+        install:

+  ascend_w8a8_mxfp8:
+    model_id: Eco-Tech/Minimax-M3.1-Flash-w8a8-mxfp8
+    label: W8A8 MXFP8 (ASCEND A5)
+    precision: mxfp8
+    supported_features:
+      - tool_calling
+      - reasoning

+    vram_minimum_gb: 514
+    description: >-

+    supported_hardware:

+    tp:

+    extra_args:

+    variants: [ascend_w8a8]

+      key: minimax-m3.1-flash-a3-agg
+      revision: '2026-11-20'
+    image:
+      vllm: quay.io/ascend/vllm-ascend:minimax-m3.1-flash-a3-openeuler
+    args:
+      - '--port'
+      - '11223'
+      - '--data-parallel-size'
+      - '4'
+      - '--enable-expert-parallel'
+      - '--max-num-seqs'
+      - '32'
+      - '--gpu-memory-utilization'
+      - '0.92'
+      - '--limit-mm-per-prompt'
+      - '{"image":1,"video":0}'
+      - '--enable-chunked-prefill'
+      - '--compilation-config'

+      - '--safetensors-load-strategy'
+      - prefetch
+    env:
+      HCCL_BUFFSIZE: '1024'
+      HCCL_IF_BASE_PORT: '61000'
+    runbook: |
+      ## Topology
+
+      One Atlas 800I A3 host with 16 Ascend 910C (64 GB each), one `vllm serve`
+      process at DP4 x TP4 x EP16. The full W8A8 checkpoint is replicated four
+      times, one replica per DP rank, TP4 within a replica.

+      One `vllm serve` per host. The decode command runs the multi-port external
+      load balancer: the supervisor process starts four child API servers per
+      host, one per local DP rank and four NPUs each, and assigns
+      `--data-parallel-start-rank` 0 (D1) / 4 (D2). Do not add
+      `--data-parallel-rank`, `--data-parallel-external-lb` or
+      `--data-parallel-hybrid-lb`; the supervisor assigns the rank per child and
+      rejects those flags. Start prefill, D1 and D2 within a few seconds of each
+      other so the DP rendezvous completes, and start the router after every
+      host prints `Application startup complete`.
+
+      ## Evidence and limits
+
+      Validated as TP4 x PP4 prefill against a global DP8 x TP4 decode group with
+      MooncakeConnectorV1 and one proxy endpoint per rank. This preset keeps the
+      validated parallelism and the same DSpark draft, and switches the launch
+      to the external-LB supervisor with MooncakeConnectorV2 (the catalog
+      default), so the tutorial's per-rank `vllm serve` loops and per-rank KV
+      port arithmetic are not needed.
+  ascend_a5_w8a8_mxfp8_pd:
+    label: 950DT MXFP8 PD (1P1D)
+    hardware: ascend_950dt_8x
+    strategy: pd_cluster
+    variants: [ascend_w8a8_mxfp8]
+    workload: Prefill/decode disaggregation, 128K context, DSpark
+    default: true
+    description: >-
+      One prefill host at DP1 x TP4 x PP2 and a distributed decode service over
+      two hosts at global DP4 x TP4, one supervisor per decode host in
+      multi-port external load-balancer mode. FP8 main-model KV cache with a
+      BF16 DSpark draft, MooncakeConnectorV2 and the Ascend Router.
+    select:
+      pd_router: ascend
+      pd_connector: mooncake_ascend
+      frontend: python
+      features:
+        text_only: true
+    source:
+      label: vLLM Ascend MiniMax-M3.1-Flash tutorial, PD on 950DT
+      href: https://docs.vllm.ai/projects/ascend/en/latest/tutorials/models/MiniMax-M3.1-Flash.html
+      key: minimax-m3.1-flash-a5-pd
+      revision: '2026-11-20'
+    image:
+      vllm: quay.io/ascend/vllm-ascend:minimax-m3.1-flash-a5-openeuler
+    # The 950DT PD scripts do not pass --hf-overrides, unlike the A3 ones.
+    roles:
+      prefill:
+        nodes: 1
+        parallelism: tep
+        pp: 2
+        args:
+          - '--dtype'
+          - bfloat16
+          - '--enforce-eager'
+          - '--max-num-seqs'
+          - '128'
+          - '--max-num-batched-tokens'
+          - '8000'
+          - '--gpu-memory-utilization'
+          - '0.85'
+          - '--kv-cache-dtype'
+          - fp8
+          - '--enable-chunked-prefill'
+          - '--safetensors-load-strategy'
+          - prefetch
+          - '--additional-config'
+          - '{"enable_cpu_binding":true,"multistream_overlap_shared_expert":true,"enable_shared_expert_dp":true,"enable_flashcomm1":true,"enable_fused_mc2":0}'
+        env:
+          VLLM_USE_FASTOKENS: '1'
+          VLLM_ENGINE_READY_TIMEOUT_S: '1800'
+          HCCL_BUFFSIZE: '512'
+          HCCL_IF_IP: $PREFILL_NODE_1
+          VLLM_HOST_IP: $PREFILL_NODE_1
+          HCCL_SOCKET_IFNAME: $IFACE_NAME
+          GLOO_SOCKET_IFNAME: $IFACE_NAME
+      decode:
+        nodes: 2
+        parallelism: dep
+        tp: 4
+        pp: 1
+        args:
+          - '--dtype'
+          - bfloat16
+          - '--max-num-seqs'
+          - '128'
+          - '--max-num-batched-tokens'
+          - '8000'
+          - '--gpu-memory-utilization'
+          - '0.92'
+          - '--kv-cache-dtype'
+          - fp8
+          - '--safetensors-load-strategy'
+          - prefetch
+          - '--seed'
+          - '1024'
+          - '--compilation-config'
+          - '{"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_DECODE_ONLY","max_cudagraph_capture_size":1024}'
+          - '--additional-config'
+          - '{"enable_cpu_binding":true,"ascend_compilation_config":{"fuse_norm_quant":false,"fuse_qknorm_rope":true},"multistream_overlap_shared_expert":true,"enable_shared_expert_dp":true,"enable_flashcomm1":true}'
+        env:
+          VLLM_ENGINE_READY_TIMEOUT_S: '1800'
+          HCCL_BUFFSIZE: '1024'
+          HCCL_IF_IP: $DECODE_NODE_1
+          VLLM_HOST_IP: $DECODE_NODE_1
+          HCCL_SOCKET_IFNAME: $IFACE_NAME
+          GLOO_SOCKET_IFNAME: $IFACE_NAME
+    runbook: |
+      ## Topology
+
+      Three Atlas 950DT hosts with eight NPUs (96 GB) each: one prefill host
+      (DP1 x TP4 x PP2) and two decode hosts sharing one global DP4 x TP4 group -
+      two local DP ranks per host, ranks 0-1 on D1 and 2-3 on D2.
+
+      ## Launch model
+
+      One `vllm serve` per host. The decode supervisor starts two child API
+      servers per host on `--port` + local rank and passes
+      `--data-parallel-start-rank` 0 (D1) / 2 (D2). Both decode hosts serve
+      HTTP; do not make D2 headless. Start the three engines within a few
+      seconds of each other; the 950DT presets raise
+      `VLLM_ENGINE_READY_TIMEOUT_S` to 1800 so the multi-host rendezvous and the
+      weight load fit in one window. Start the router after every host prints
+      `Application startup complete`.
+
+      ## Evidence and limits
+
+      Validated as TP4 x PP2 prefill against global DP4 x TP4 decode with
+      MooncakeConnectorV1, FP8 main-model KV cache and a BF16 DSpark draft. This
+      preset keeps the parallelism, the KV dtypes and the 1024-token graph
+      capture, and switches the launch to the external-LB supervisor with
+      MooncakeConnectorV2. For 16K-input workloads the tutorial halves
+      `max-num-seqs` to 64 and drops `max_cudagraph_capture_size`; that variant
+      is not a separate preset.
+hardware_notes:
+  ascend_910c:
+    title: Atlas 800I A3 runs the W8A8 ModelScope build with 100g of shm
+    body: >-
+      Verified on Atlas 800I A3 (16 x Ascend 910C, 64 GB HBM per NPU) with
+      quay.io/ascend/vllm-ascend:minimax-m3.1-flash-a3-openeuler. The weights are
+      Eco-Tech/Minimax-M3.1-Flash-w8a8 from ModelScope; the recipe sets
+      VLLM_USE_MODELSCOPE and passes --quantization ascend, and no model revision
+      is pinned because the tutorial pins none. The Docker command starts the
+      container with 100g of shared memory, --network host and --privileged. The
+      Ascend deployment guide below covers the PD placeholders, the minimal
+      decode launch and the ports.
+    link:
+      label: Ascend deployment
+      href: '#ascend-deployment'
+  ascend_950dt_8x:
+    title: Atlas 950DT runs the W8A8 MXFP8 build with CCU_SCHED expansion
+    body: >-
+      Verified on Atlas 950DT (8 NPUs, 96 GB HBM each) with
+      quay.io/ascend/vllm-ascend:minimax-m3.1-flash-a5-openeuler. The weights are
+      Eco-Tech/Minimax-M3.1-Flash-w8a8-mxfp8 from ModelScope, again with
+      --quantization ascend and no pinned revision. The generated Docker command
+      sets 100g of shared memory, --network host and --privileged; add
+      --ipc host yourself because the recipe cannot express extra Docker flags.
+      The PD presets use an FP8 main-model KV cache with a BF16 DSpark draft; the
+      Ascend deployment guide lists the rest.
+    link:
+      label: Ascend deployment
+      href: '#ascend-deployment'
+notes:
+  - title: Ascend PD requires the qualified preset
+    when:
+      hardware: [ascend_910c, ascend_950dt_8x]
+      strategies: [pd_cluster]
+    body: >-
+      The prefill/decode cost model and role sizing in Baseline, Dynamo, SMG and
+      the vLLM router do not describe the validated Ascend 1P1D lanes. Use the
+      A3 or 950DT PD preset, which pins the prefill TP/PP split, the global
+      decode DP group, the Ascend Router and MooncakeConnectorV2 on both pools.
+guide_sections:
+  ascend: |
+    ### Ascend deployment
+
+    MiniMax M3.1-Flash on Ascend runs from ModelScope builds of the
+    quantization-aware checkpoint: `Eco-Tech/Minimax-M3.1-Flash-w8a8` on Atlas
+    800I A3 (16 x Ascend 910C, 64 GB HBM per NPU) and
+    `Eco-Tech/Minimax-M3.1-Flash-w8a8-mxfp8` on Atlas 950DT (8 NPUs, 96 GB each).
+    The Hugging Face checkpoint `MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3.1-Flash` stores NVFP4
+    experts and does not run on NPU; both Ascend builds need
+    `--quantization ascend`. No model revision is pinned, matching the tutorial.
+
+    The two images are model-specific builds. Each Docker command starts the
+    container with `--network host --privileged --shm-size=100g`; the 950DT
+    container also needs `--ipc host`. The recipe sets the shared-memory size for
+    you.
+
+    | Lane | Preset |
+    | --- | --- |
+    | A3, 128K context, DP4 x TP4 / EP16, one host | `ascend_a3_w8a8_agg` |
+    | 950DT, 128K context, DP2 x TP4 / EP8, one host | `ascend_a5_w8a8_mxfp8_agg` |
+    | A3, 1P1D, prefill DP1 x TP4 x PP4 + decode DP8 x TP4 over two hosts | `ascend_a3_w8a8_pd` |
+    | 950DT, 1P1D, prefill DP1 x TP4 x PP2 + decode DP4 x TP4 over two hosts | `ascend_a5_w8a8_mxfp8_pd` |
+
+    Each PD preset is the default for the `pd_cluster` strategy on its hardware;
+    it needs three hosts and the Ascend Router. The single-node presets remain
+    the defaults for the single-node strategy.
+
+    **Placeholders in the generated commands.** The PD lanes carry six shell
+    variables; substitute them before launch:
+
+    - `$PREFILL_NODE_1` — the prefill host's address on the interface the decode
+      hosts and the router can reach.
+    - `$DECODE_NODE_1` — the first decode host, and the address of the global DP
+      group: both decode hosts pass it as `--data-parallel-address`, and the
+      rank-0 child API server on D1 binds the DP coordination endpoint there.
+      The supervisor process itself only serves the aggregated `/health`.
+    - `$DECODE_NODE_2` — the second decode host's own address, used for its
+      `HCCL_IF_IP` and `VLLM_HOST_IP`. It is not the DP address: every decode
+      host keeps `--data-parallel-address $DECODE_NODE_1`.
+    - `$DECODE_DP_RPC_PORT` — a free TCP port for the DP rendezvous, reachable
+      from both decode hosts and not bound by any other pool (for example 16920
+      on A3 and 6885 on 950DT, the values the tutorial uses).
+    - `$ROUTER_PORT` — the Ascend Router's listening port; the command builder
+      supplies a default, and the tutorial's proxy uses 19080. Make sure it is
+      free on the host that runs the router.
+    - `$IFACE_NAME` — the business NIC on that host, for `HCCL_SOCKET_IFNAME` and
+      `GLOO_SOCKET_IFNAME`. The recipe leaves `HCCL_IF_IP`, `VLLM_HOST_IP`, and
+      the socket variables explicit on every PD role because a multi-homed host
+      needs them to agree; the single-node presets do not set them.
+
+    Every other port is literal: prefill HTTP 8001, decode `--port` 8002, KV
+    transfer 36000 (prefill) and 36100 (decode).
+
+    **Prefill.** One `vllm serve` process per role, TP4 with PP4 (A3) or PP2
+    (950DT) and expert parallelism across the node, `--language-model-only`,
+    eager main model, and a DSpark draft on both pools. The A3 role exports
+    `VLLM_PP_LAYER_PARTITION=15,15,15,15` (the model has 60 layers, so this is
+    also the even split) and `ASCEND_LOCAL_COMM_RES`; unset the partition
+    variable before starting any other lane on the same shell. Before launch,
+    run `unset HCCL_INTRA_ROCE_ENABLE` on the A3 PD hosts: the tutorial requires
+    it and it cannot be expressed as a recipe environment variable.
+
+    **A3 `ASCEND_LOCAL_COMM_RES`.** This variable selects the HIXL local
+    communication resource for the HCCS fabric and must be the JSON string
+    `{"version":"1.2"}`. The recipe renderer currently emits environment values
+    without shell quotes, so the copied A3 PD command passes `{version:1.2}`
+    and HIXL cannot parse it. Until the renderer is fixed, quote it by hand: in
+    the bare command, export `ASCEND_LOCAL_COMM_RES='{"version":"1.2"}'`; in
+    the Docker command, remove the generated `-e ASCEND_LOCAL_COMM_RES=...` and
+    pass `-e ASCEND_LOCAL_COMM_RES` after that export. The 950DT lanes do not
+    set this variable.
+
+    **Decode.** One `vllm serve` supervisor per decode host, not one process per
+    rank. Both PD presets use vLLM's multi-port external load balancer: the
+    supervisor starts one child API server per local DP rank, each child owning
+    TP4 worth of NPUs, and it assigns `--data-parallel-start-rank` 0 (A3 D1), 4
+    (A3 D2), 0 (950DT D1) and 2 (950DT D2). A3 therefore serves children on
+    8002-8005 per host and 950DT on 8002-8003; the supervisor publishes
+    aggregated `/health` on vLLM's default port 9256, and
+    `--data-parallel-supervisor-port` moves only that health port. Do not add
+    `--data-parallel-rank`, `--data-parallel-external-lb` or
+    `--data-parallel-hybrid-lb`: the supervisor assigns ranks to children and
+    rejects those flags. Both decode hosts serve HTTP, so do not make the second
+    one headless.
+
+    The decode graph capture sizes are not cosmetic: at 128 sequences and seven
+    draft tokens an A3 decode step holds 1024 tokens while that lane captures
+    512, and the 950DT lane captures 1024. With 64 sequences the default limit
+    is enough, which is why the 16K-input variant of the tutorial drops
+    `max_cudagraph_capture_size` instead of raising it.
+
+    **KV transfer.** Both pools use `MooncakeConnectorV2` (the catalog default
+    for `mooncake_ascend`) instead of the tutorial's `MooncakeConnectorV1`
+    config. The `kv_port` is the base side-channel port and the connector
+    derives the per-rank ports from the device index, so the tutorial's
+    `25000 + rank * 32` arithmetic is not needed. Keep
+    `kv_connector_extra_config` in sync with the tp/pp/dp flags if you change
+    the topology: the recipe fills the pool shapes from the rendered roles. A
+    tp or dp mismatch fails fast at startup with a `ValueError`; `pp` is not
+    part of that check, so a pp mismatch can surface later as a KV handshake
+    failure.
+
+    **Startup order.** Start prefill, D1 and D2 within a few seconds of each
+    other - a role started later blocks the distributed rendezvous, and the
+    roles started earlier fail when their ready timeout expires. On 950DT the
+    presets raise `VLLM_ENGINE_READY_TIMEOUT_S` to 1800 for the weight load and
+    multi-host rendezvous. Start the Ascend Router only after every host prints
+    `Application startup complete`, and point it at the prefill child (8001) and
+    at every decode child (8002-8005 or 8002-8003 on both decode hosts); a
+    single decode endpoint per host leaves the other local ranks idle.
+
+    **Features.** DSpark speculative decoding (seven tokens, eager draft, BF16
+    draft KV) is on in every lane. Tool calling is on for the A3 single-node and
+    950DT PD lanes and off for the A3 PD and 950DT single-node lanes, exactly as
+    in the tutorial; the MiniMax reasoning parser is on everywhere. Both PD
+    lanes load text only (`--language-model-only`). The A3 PD preset also passes
+    `--hf-overrides` with the sparse architecture its scripts use; the 950DT PD
+    scripts do not pass it, so that preset does not either.
+
+    **Not covered here.** The A2 two-node colocated layout (section 5.2), the KV
+    cache pool with `MultiConnector` (section 5.4), the 1M-token PD layout
+    (section 5.5) and the 16K-input decode variant (64 sequences, default graph
+    capture) stay in the tutorial. The per-rank `vllm serve` scripts of section
+    5.3 are replaced by the supervisor; the Python load-balance proxy is now
+    launched as the catalog's Ascend Router, which runs the same
+    `load_balance_proxy_server_example.py` from the image.

[Doc][Recipe] Add Qwen3.8-Flash-Next presets for A3 and 950DT (#22454)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

Add Ascend deployment presets for Qwen3.8-Flash-Next from the model
tutorial, covering single-host A3 and 950DT workers.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

- A2 and A3 share the W4A8 checkpoint. The A2 and A3 hardware selections
apply their respective container images and launch parameters.
- A3 splits devices 0–7 and 8–15. Choose the image-and-text 10K Prefill
and Decode points in the A3 single-host PD preset. The A3 command card
includes the full four-rank Decode launcher, proxy and multimodal
request.
- 950DT splits devices 0–3 and 4–7. The 950DT single-host PD preset
pairs Prefill and Decode points for basic PD, multimodal and
long-context workloads.
- Generated worker containers set shared memory to 128g on A3 and 500g
on 950DT.

Under Tensor Parallel, each hardware has one single-host PD preset.
Select the two points for the same workload and run both roles on that
host. The guide links the corresponding proxy commands. For MemCache
three-tier pooling, follow Sections 4.3 and 5.5 of the deployment
tutorial for storage preparation, pool configuration, MetaService and
P/D startup. [Deployment guide at the reviewed
revision](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/blob/a41e2ff8ba274328f9ef2ff27d15653df1d2e8ee/docs/source/tutorials/models/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next.md)

### Recipe preview

| [Image Decode and four-rank
launcher](https://vllm-recipes-git-preview-vllm-ascend-pr-22454-inferact-inc.vercel.app/Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next?hardware=ascend_910c&variant=ascend_w4a8&strategy=single_node_tp&preset=a3_single_host_pd&point=image_10k_decode)

| [Basic
Decode](https://vllm-recipes-git-preview-vllm-ascend-pr-22454-inferact-inc.vercel.app/Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next?hardware=ascend_950dt&variant=ascend_a5_w4a8_mxfp&strategy=single_node_tp&preset=a5_single_host_pd&point=basic_decode)
|

### How was this patch tested?

Strict assembly, schema validation and JSON API generation passed with
recipes renderer cb7c0e949bcb2bf580fcbd0d1d4e2e69ebf502ee. Compared 24
selections before and after sharing the W4A8 variant, including the
inherited A2 PD preset, all A3 and 950DT workload points, and
representative NVIDIA and AMD hardware. The generated launch arguments,
environments and Docker commands matched. The Ascend configuration check
covered 21 scenarios with zero errors and eight warnings.

Checked that the four MemCache pooling points were removed and all
remaining presets and points match the previous revision. The A3
image-and-text Decode loop was previously dry-run against Section 5.3
for all four ranks.

### Checklist

- [x] Reviewed worker device slices, rank-specific ports, shared-memory
sizes and long-context token limits.
- [x] Compared rendered parameters with their documented workloads.

+notes:
+  - title: A3 image-and-text 10K launch scripts
+    when:
+      hardware: [ascend_910c]
+      variants: [ascend_w4a8]
+      strategies: [single_node_tp]
+    body: |
+      Use these scripts only for the **Image and text (10K) / Prefill** and **Image and text (10K) / Decode** points of the A3 single-host PD preset. Run Prefill, Decode and the proxy in separate terminals inside the prepared A3 container.
+
+      **Environment for Prefill and Decode** — run this block in both worker terminals.
+
+      ```bash
+      local_ip="<LOCAL_SERVICE_IP>"
+      nic_name="<SERVICE_NETWORK_INTERFACE>"
+
+      unset ftp_proxy FTP_PROXY https_proxy HTTPS_PROXY http_proxy HTTP_PROXY all_proxy ALL_PROXY
+      export VLLM_HOST_IP="${local_ip}"
+      export HCCL_IF_IP="${local_ip}"
+      export GLOO_SOCKET_IFNAME="${nic_name}"
+      export TP_SOCKET_IFNAME="${nic_name}"
+      export HCCL_SOCKET_IFNAME="${nic_name}"
+      export no_proxy="localhost,127.0.0.1,${local_ip}"
+      export NO_PROXY="${no_proxy}"
+      export LD_LIBRARY_PATH="$(python -c 'import mooncake; print(next(iter(mooncake.__path__)))'):${LD_LIBRARY_PATH:-}"
+      export VLLM_USE_MODELSCOPE=True
+      export VLLM_SERVER_DEV_MODE=1
+      export VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1
+      export VLLM_EXECUTE_MODEL_TIMEOUT_SECONDS=3000
+      export VLLM_ENGINE_READY_TIMEOUT_S=2400
+      export VLLM_ASCEND_PLE_BACKEND=torch
+      ```
+
+      **Prefill** — run on devices 0–7.
+
+      ```bash
+      export ASCEND_RT_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1,2,3,4,5,6,7
+      export HCCL_NPU_SOCKET_PORT_RANGE=61400-61499
+      export HCCL_BUFFSIZE=4096
+      export VLLM_PP_LAYER_PARTITION=24,24
+
+      vllm serve Eco-Tech/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-w4a8 \
+          --host 0.0.0.0 \
+          --port 25568 \
+          --served-model-name qwen38-flash-next-a3-pd \
+          --trust-remote-code \
+          --mm-encoder-tp-mode data \
+          --quantization ascend \
+          --tensor-parallel-size 4 \
+          --pipeline-parallel-size 2 \
+          --data-parallel-size 1 \
+          --data-parallel-size-local 1 \
+          --max-model-len 262144 \
+          --max-num-seqs 32 \
+          --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 \
+          --gpu-memory-utilization 0.90 \
+          --no-enable-prefix-caching \
+          --async-scheduling \
+          --enable-expert-parallel \
+          --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode":"NONE"}' \
+          --engram-config '{"cpu_offload":true,"dp_shared_memory":false}' \
+          --additional-config '{"enable_shared_expert_dp":false,"enable_flashcomm1":true,"enable_prefill_mc2":true,"enable_fused_mc2":0,"enable_cpu_binding":true,"multistream_overlap_shared_expert":true,"ascend_compilation_config":{"fuse_norm_quant":false}}' \
+          --speculative-config '{"method":"qwen3_5_mtp","num_speculative_tokens":3,"enforce_eager":true}' \
+          --kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"MooncakeConnectorV2","kv_role":"kv_producer","kv_port":"34600","kv_connector_extra_config":{"prefill":{"dp_size":1,"tp_size":4,"pp_size":2,"pp_layer_partition":"24,24"},"decode":{"dp_size":4,"tp_size":2}}}'
+      ```
+
+      **Decode** — run this entire block once in the Decode terminal. It starts four TP2 workers in the same container. Keep the terminal open while they run.
+
+      ```bash
+      unset VLLM_PP_LAYER_PARTITION
+      export HCCL_NPU_SOCKET_PORT_RANGE=61500-61599
+      export HCCL_BUFFSIZE=512
+
+      for DECODE_RANK in 0 1 2 3; do
+          first_device=$((8 + DECODE_RANK * 2))
+          DECODE_HTTP_PORT=$((25569 + DECODE_RANK * 10))
+          kv_port=$((32700 + DECODE_RANK * 20))
+
+          DECODE_DEVICES="${first_device},$((first_device + 1))"
+          DECODE_KV_CONFIG='{"kv_connector":"MooncakeConnectorV2","kv_role":"kv_consumer","kv_port":"'"$kv_port"'","kv_connector_extra_config":{"prefill":{"dp_size":1,"tp_size":4,"pp_size":2,"pp_layer_partition":"24,24"},"decode":{"dp_size":4,"tp_size":2}}}'
+
+          ASCEND_RT_VISIBLE_DEVICES="${DECODE_DEVICES}" \
+          vllm serve Eco-Tech/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-w4a8 \
+              --host 0.0.0.0 \
+              --port "${DECODE_HTTP_PORT}" \
+              --served-model-name qwen38-flash-next-a3-pd \
+              --trust-remote-code \
+              --quantization ascend \
+              --tensor-parallel-size 2 \
+              --data-parallel-size 4 \
+              --data-parallel-size-local 1 \
+              --data-parallel-rank "${DECODE_RANK}" \
+              --data-parallel-address "${local_ip}" \
+              --data-parallel-rpc-port 29569 \
+              --max-model-len 262144 \
+              --max-num-seqs 32 \
+              --max-num-batched-tokens 4096 \
+              --gpu-memory-utilization 0.90 \
+              --no-enable-prefix-caching \
+              --async-scheduling \
+              --enable-expert-parallel \
+              --engram-config '{"cpu_offload":true,"dp_shared_memory":true}' \
+              --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_DECODE_ONLY"}' \
+              --additional-config '{"enable_flashcomm1":true,"enable_cpu_binding":true,"enable_shared_expert_dp":true,"multistream_overlap_shared_expert":true,"scheduler_config":{"recompute_scheduler_enable":true},"ascend_compilation_config":{"fuse_norm_quant":false,"enable_npugraph_ex":true,"enable_static_kernel":true,"enable_super_kernel":false}}' \
+              --speculative-config '{"method":"qwen3_5_mtp","num_speculative_tokens":3}' \
+              --kv-transfer-config "${DECODE_KV_CONFIG}" &
+      done
+      wait
+      ```
+
+      **Proxy** — run from the vLLM-Ascend repository root in the third terminal. This checks all five endpoints before starting the proxy.
+
+      ```bash
+      local_ip="<LOCAL_SERVICE_IP>"
+
+      unset ftp_proxy FTP_PROXY https_proxy HTTPS_PROXY http_proxy HTTP_PROXY all_proxy ALL_PROXY
+      export no_proxy="localhost,127.0.0.1,${local_ip}"
+      export NO_PROXY="${no_proxy}"
+
+      for port in 25568 25569 25579 25589 25599; do
+          curl --fail --noproxy '*' "http://${local_ip}:${port}/v1/models" || exit 1
+      done
+
+      python examples/disaggregated_prefill_v1/load_balance_proxy_server_example.py \
+          --host 0.0.0.0 --port 25570 \
+          --prefiller-hosts "${local_ip}" --prefiller-ports 25568 \
+          --decoder-hosts "${local_ip}" "${local_ip}" "${local_ip}" "${local_ip}" \
+          --decoder-ports 25569 25579 25589 25599
+      ```
+
+      **Verify through the proxy** — once the proxy is listening, run this request in another terminal on the same host. Replace `<IMAGE_URL>` with an image URL both workers can access and `<TEXT_PROMPT>` with the text for your 10K sample.
+

+          -d '{"model":"qwen38-flash-next-a3-pd","messages":[{"role":"user","content":[{"type":"image_url","image_url":{"url":"<IMAGE_URL>"}},{"type":"text","text":"<TEXT_PROMPT>"}]}],"max_tokens":1024,"temperature":0}'
+      ```

+
+    The 950DT Basic PD presets use the tutorial's `VLLM_VERSION=0.32.0` override with the
+    `v0.32.0rc1-a5` image. If you switch images, unset this override so vLLM Ascend
+    detects the installed vLLM version.
+
+    For basic, image or long-context serving, prepare the hardware-specific container
+    using the [A3 Docker script](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/blob/a41e2ff8ba274328f9ef2ff27d15653df1d2e8ee/docs/source/tutorials/models/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next.md?plain=1#L84-L123) or the [950DT Docker script](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/blob/a41e2ff8ba274328f9ef2ff27d15653df1d2e8ee/docs/source/tutorials/models/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next.md?plain=1#L125-L162) in Section 4.1.
+    Set `LOCAL_SERVICE_IP` and `SERVICE_NIC` to the service address
+    and interface. In each role shell, initialize CANN/ATB, unset proxy variables
+    and any inherited `VLLM_PP_LAYER_PARTITION`, and add Mooncake to the library path:
+
+    ```bash
+    export LD_LIBRARY_PATH="$(python -c 'import mooncake; print(next(iter(mooncake.__path__)))'):${LD_LIBRARY_PATH:-}"
+    ```
+
+    Run the two generated serve commands with their respective environments in separate
+    shells inside that container. Start the proxy from the vLLM-Ascend repository
+    root once both role endpoints respond at `/v1/models`.
+
+    | Basic PD | Prefill HTTP | Decode HTTP | Proxy HTTP |
+    | --- | --- | --- | --- |
+    | A3 | 25568 | 25569 | 25570 |
+    | 950DT | 8088 | 8092 | 8087 |
+
+    ```bash
+    # A3. For 950DT, set these ports to 8088, 8092 and 8087.
+    PREFILL_PORT=25568
+    DECODE_PORT=25569
+    PROXY_PORT=25570
+    python examples/disaggregated_prefill_v1/load_balance_proxy_server_example.py \
+        --host 0.0.0.0 --port "${PROXY_PORT}" \
+        --prefiller-hosts "${LOCAL_SERVICE_IP}" --prefiller-ports "${PREFILL_PORT}" \
+        --decoder-hosts "${LOCAL_SERVICE_IP}" --decoder-ports "${DECODE_PORT}"
+    ```
+
+    Use the proxy ports in the linked procedure for each workload point.
+    Both long-context roles use YaRN and a 1,010,000-token service limit.
+
+    #### MemCache three-tier pooling on A3 and 950DT
+
+    Use the model deployment tutorial for the complete pooling procedure, including the Prefill and Decode commands.
+
+    1. Before starting the container, prepare the SSD or loop devices and mount them together with the MemCache configuration directory as shown in [Section 4.3, Docker for three-tier PD pooling](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/blob/a41e2ff8ba274328f9ef2ff27d15653df1d2e8ee/docs/source/tutorials/models/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next.md#43-docker-for-three-tier-pd-pooling).
+    2. In [Section 5.5, PD separation with a MemCache three-tier KV cache pool](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/blob/a41e2ff8ba274328f9ef2ff27d15653df1d2e8ee/docs/source/tutorials/models/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next.md#55-pd-separation-with-memcache-three-tier-kv-cache-pool), select your hardware. For a new pool, configure the MetaService and LocalService files and start MetaService. For an existing pool, use its endpoints and LocalService files and preserve its disk initialization settings.
+    3. Confirm the MetaService and ConfigStore endpoints are reachable, then use the service environment and P/D launch commands in the same hardware tab.

[Doc][Recipe] Add DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash 950DT 1P1D recipe (#22575)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

Publish the v0.32 RC DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash MXFP recipe for Ascend 950DT in
a separate PR from the A3 recipe in #20065. The preset serves one
Prefill node and one Decode node. Each node has eight NPUs and uses
DP8/TP1 with expert parallelism. Both worker groups use
`--data-parallel-multi-port-external-lb`, and `MooncakeHybridConnector`
transfers KV directly between the groups.

### Does this PR introduce any user-facing change?

The vLLM Recipes command builder gains a 950DT preset for non-pooling
1P1D. The existing Ascend deployment tutorial documents the scenario.
This PR adds the recipe and leaves the released serving code unchanged.

### How was this patch tested?

- Ran the standard Recipes source validator against
`vllm-project/recipes@04e4698`. Strict assembly, schema validation, and
JSON API generation passed.
- Compared the rendered Prefill, Decode, and Router commands with the
950DT preset in #20065. Verified DP8/TP1, eight HTTP endpoints per role,
and `512g` container shared memory. The A2 render matched `main`.
- `git diff --check` passed. NPU deployment validation is pending.

- vLLM main:
https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/c410543d9ffff03f5f6c4a8c0ae1d3ad082c4a15

---------

Signed-off-by: rikakuhi <942697235@qq.com>
